issues.title: Grass/foliage color overrides applied by Fabric API's BiomeModifications are ignored (stale cache in BiomeMixin)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

A grass color override set through Fabric API's BiomeModifications is never rendered while Sodium is installed. Grass uses the default color from the climate map instead. The same override renders correctly without Sodium, and on a vanilla client connected to a server that applies the override.

**Cause**
- Sodium's BiomeMixin (fabric module) reads specialEffects.grassColorOverride() and foliageColorOverride() in setupColors(). That runs from the Biome constructor and caches hasCustomGrassColor and customGrassColor.
- getGrassColor and getFoliageColor only call setupColors() again when this.specialEffects != this.cachedSpecialEffects.
- Fabric API's BiomeModificationContextImpl.EffectsContextImpl.setGrassColorOverride runs after the constructor and mutates the existing BiomeSpecialEffects instance in place (effects.grassColorOverride = ...). The reference never changes, so the cache is never refreshed.
- setGrassColorModifier, setFoliageColorOverride and the other effects setters are mutated the same way, so they are probably affected too.

Expected: the grass is red (0x821f1f).

Actual: the grass is the default yellow-ish green from the climate map. F3+A doesn't help. Removing Sodium makes the color appear.

I'm also filing a matching issue against Fabric API, since it mutates the effects in place: https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-api/issues/5637

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install Sodium 0.9.2, Fabric API 0.161.0 and a mod that sets a grass override on an existing biome, a minimal example is:
```
BiomeModifications.create(id("test"))
    .add(ModificationPhase.REPLACEMENTS,
         BiomeSelectors.includeByKey(Biomes.NETHER_WASTES),
         ctx -> ctx.getEffects().setGrassColorOverride(0x821f1f));
```
2. Create a world and go to the modified biome.
3. Look at grass in that biome.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33158592/latest.log)

### Crash Report

[crash-2026-10-07_16.38.24-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33159110/crash-2026-10-07_16.38.24-client.txt)

issues.title: FRAPI: copyFrom() and load() don't restore normalFace, causing "facing is null" NPE in BakedChunkModelBuilder
issues.body:
### Bug Description

**Versions**
- Minecraft 26.3, Fabric
- Sodium 0.9.2+mc26.3 (also 0.9.3-alpha.1)
- Triggered by Terrain Slabs 3.4.1 (uses Fabric Renderer API mesh + emitter.copyFrom)

**Crash**
NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "ModelQuadFacing.ordinal()" because "facing" is null
at BakedChunkModelBuilder.getVertexBuffer(BakedChunkModelBuilder.java:24)
at BlockRenderer.bufferQuad(BlockRenderer.java:181)
...
at MutableQuadViewWrapper.emit(MutableQuadViewWrapper.java:226)
Crash report attached.

**Cause**
In MutableQuadViewImpl.copyFrom(QuadViewImpl q), isGeometryInvalid and faceNormal are copied from
the source, but normalFace is not. Similarly, QuadViewImpl.load() sets isGeometryInvalid = false
without setting normalFace. As a result, normalFace() returns whatever value the emitter last held
without recomputing it. That value is stale, or null on a fresh emitter (e.g. a newly started
chunk-builder thread after a world load).

A mod that copies a mesh quad into the emitter and emits it without changing vertex positions hits
this. In practice it crashes deterministically when reloading a world near the affected blocks.

**Suggested fix**
- In copyFrom: when the geometry is valid, also copy `this.normalFace = q.normalFace;`
- In load(): set `this.normalFace = ModelQuadFacing.fromPackedNormal(this.packedFaceNormal());`
  (or simply leave isGeometryInvalid = true so computeGeometry() runs)

### Reproduction Steps

1. Fabric 26.3 with Sodium 0.9.2+mc26.3 (same issue with 0.9.3 alpha) and Terrain Slabs 3.4.1
   (plus its dependencies, Architectury API and MidnightLib).
   Full mod list is in the attached log; my instance also has Iris, Distant Horizons,
   Tectonic, Terralith and Wilder Wild.
2. Create a world and go to terrain where Terrain Slabs has generated slabs with
   blocks sitting on or next to them (snow layers and tall grass both triggered it;
   snowy mountain slopes trigger it most reliably).
3. Stand next to those blocks, save and quit to the title screen, then reload the world.
4. The game crashes while building chunk meshes ("facing" is null). In my world it crashes
   on every reload at about X -624, Y 448, Z 1810, so the world can no longer be opened.

Notes:
- Flying around in the same terrain during a session does NOT crash. It only happens
  right after the world loads, which matches normalFace being null on a freshly started
  chunk-builder thread (see the cause section).
- Happens on both 0.9.2 and 0.9.3-alpha.1.
- I can provide the world save, which reproduces it 100% of the time on load.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33088430/latest.log)

### Crash Report

[crash-2026-10-06_16.03.02-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33088433/crash-2026-10-06_16.03.02-client.txt)

issues.title: Terrain briefly flashes pale when leaving water (Sodium 0.9.2, Minecraft 26.1.2)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

When moving out of water, the terrain briefly flashes pale blue/white and then returns to normal. The HUD and held hand are unaffected. The flash is particularly noticeable in caves. Expected behavior is a normal fog transition without the flash.

The issue occurs with official, unmodified Sodium as the only installed mod. In the same instance and world, disabling Sodium removed the flash in the control recording. The game settings were unchanged.

### Environment

- Minecraft: 26.1.2
- Fabric Loader: 0.19.5
- Sodium: official, unmodified 0.9.2; the only top-level mod JAR
- OS: Windows
- GPU: AMD Radeon 880M
- Shaders: none
- Resource packs: none

These screenshots are frames extracted from the recordings. The Sodium recording shows flashes at approximately 6.8 s and 9.8 s; repeated water transitions in the recording without Sodium did not show the same flash.

### Screenshots

**With Sodium:** consecutive frames from left to right at 6.800 s, 6.817 s, and 6.833 s. The middle frame shows the pale terrain flash; the hand and HUD are unaffected.

![With Sodium: normal underwater frame, pale terrain flash, normal air frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2141565b-aea7-4c60-8bb4-fa494993861c)

**Without Sodium:** consecutive frames from the control recording at 7.750 s, 7.767 s, and 7.783 s. This water-to-air transition has no pale terrain flash.

![Without Sodium: three consecutive frames during a normal water-to-air transition](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7c06c1c-35c4-4fa7-a024-04e39855bc54)

## Reproduction Steps

1. Go to a water boundary with nearby terrain in view. A cave can make the flash easier to see.
2. Repeatedly move into and out of the water.
3. When leaving the water, the terrain may briefly turn pale before returning to normal.

## Crash Report

No crash occurred, so there is no crash report.

issues.title: [1.21.1] Polytone compound biome colors don't work
Quads without baked normals render dark with smooth lighting on NeoForge
issues.body:
### Bug Description

On NeoForge, quads baked without normals (`BakedNormals.UNSPECIFIED`, which is what the plain 10-arg `BakedQuad` constructor gives you) render really dark with smooth lighting on if they aren't axis-aligned. Flat lighting looks fine.

I think it's because `BakedQuadMixin.getVertexNormal` returns `-1` for unspecified normals:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/mc26.1.2-0.9.2/neoforge/src/mod/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/mixin/core/model/quad/BakedQuadMixin.java#L95

but `MutableQuadViewImpl.fromVanillaInternal` only treats `0` as "no normal":

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/mc26.1.2-0.9.2/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/model/MutableQuadViewImpl.java#L278

So every vertex gets a normal of about (-0.008, -0.008, -0.008) and `getAccurateNormal` never falls back to the face normal. `applyIrregularFace` then weights each axis by the normal squared, which adds up to almost nothing, so the `* 0.5f` at the end ends up cutting both the brightness and the light level in half:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/mc26.1.2-0.9.2/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/model/light/smooth/SmoothLightPipeline.java#L314-L315

Returning `0` there (same as `BakedNormals.UNSPECIFIED.normal(i)`) should fix it. It's still the same on `dev`.

Vanilla blocks don't run into this since regular cube faces never take the irregular path. We hit it with the infusion pillars in Thaumaturge, which have slanted faces. We've worked around it on our end by baking normals, but any mod using the short constructor will see it.

Sodium 0.9.2 for 26.1.2, NeoForge 26.1.2.76.

### Reproduction Steps

1. On NeoForge 26.1.2, make a block model with a slanted quad built with `new BakedQuad(p0, p1, p2, p3, uv0, uv1, uv2, uv3, direction, materialInfo)` (no normals).
2. Place the block with smooth lighting on.
3. The slanted faces come out way darker than they should. Turn smooth lighting off or remove Sodium and they look normal.

### Log File

Not attaching one since nothing shows up in the log for this, but I can grab one if you need it.

### Crash Report

Same as above, happy to add one if needed.

issues.title: Fix fluid side mapping so it points to the center of the texture
issues.body: ### Request Description In vanilla, the side textures of water and lava map the upper-left quarter of the texture, rather than the center (https://mojira.dev/MC-267861). This was reported under #2471 which was marked as fixed earlier this year, however using this resource pack [test-pack-for-water.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32764730/test-pack-for-water.zip) reveals that the issue still persists. To fix this, water and lava should map the center of the water_flow and lava_flow textures, rather than one of the corners. In order to avoid #3523 this should only happen for water if that face isn't behind glass or a similar such block.

issues.title: RadixSort.sortIndirect orders keys as unsigned, disagreeing with its own fallback path and documented contract
issues.body:
### Disclosure first

This was found with AI assistance. Per `CONTRIBUTING.md` I've closed the PR I opened (#3925) and I'm **not** proposing a patch here — no code, just the defect and how to observe it, so you can fix it however you see fit. If AI-assisted bug reports are also unwelcome, say so and I'll close this and stop.

### Summary

`RadixSort.extractDigit` buckets digits with an unsigned shift:

```java
private static int extractDigit(int key, int digit) {
    return ((key >>> (digit * DIGIT_BITS)) & DIGIT_MASK);
}
```

so the 4-pass LSD sort orders keys as **unsigned**. But:

- the `perm.length <= RADIX_SORT_THRESHOLD` fallback, `IntArrays.quickSortIndirect`, orders them **signed**;
- the `catch (OutOfMemoryError)` path does too;
- `sortIndirect`'s own javadoc promises *"natural ascending order"* with `x[perm[i]] < x[perm[i + 1]]`.

So for any key set containing keys with bit 31 set, `sortIndirect` returns two different orderings depending only on whether the array is longer than 80 elements.

### Why the keys are signed

`MathUtil.floatToComparableInt` returns `bits ^ ((bits >> 31) & 0x7FFFFFFF)`, which leaves bit 31 **set** for negative floats — so the encoding is ordered for *signed* comparison. Its javadoc claims the opposite:

> The resulting integer can be treated as if it's unsigned and numbers the floats from the smallest negative to the largest positive value.

That sentence is the inaccurate one, and it looks like the origin of the mismatch. Concretely:

```
f=-1.0 -> key 0xC07FFFFF ;  f=1.0 -> key 0x3F800000
  signed  : -1065353217 < 1065353216  -> true   (correct)
  unsigned :  3229614079 < 1065353216  -> false  (-1.0 sorts AFTER +1.0)
```

Checked across 299,028 distinct `float32` values plus all 255 exponent boundaries with both signs, including ±inf, ±0 and subnormals: **0** signed-monotonicity violations. Under unsigned there is exactly one violating adjacent pair — at zero — but that single crossing moves the whole negative half-line to the top of the result.

`InnerPartitionBSPNode` already states the intent: *"Encoding with `floatToComparableInt` is necessary here to ensure negative distances are not sorted backwards."*

### Which call sites can see it

`TQuad.getAlignedDotProduct` returns `extents[facing.ordinal()] * facing.getSign()`, so every `NEG_*` facing yields a negative plane distance and every `POS_*` a positive one.

| call site | mixed-sign keys? |
|---|---|
| `StaticNormalRelativeData.fromDoubleUnaligned` | **yes** — selected when `alignedFacingBitmap == 0`, i.e. normals `n` and `-n` sorted together in one global pass, so both signs are present by construction |
| `InnerPartitionBSPNode.buildSNRLeafNodeFromQuads` | **yes** |
| `StaticNormalRelativeData.fromMixed` | aligned groups are single-signed; the unaligned group can mix |
| `VertexSorters.orthographicZ` | **yes** (`~floatToComparableInt(-z)`) |
| `DynamicTopoData` | no — `~floatToRawIntBits(distanceSquared)` is always negative |
| `VertexSorters` distance metrics | no — always negative |

The last two matter for scoping: keys that are all one sign sort identically under both conventions, so those paths are unaffected either way.

### Observed

I compiled the unmodified `RadixSort.java` and `MathUtil.java` on Temurin 21 against real `fastutil` 8.5.15 and `joml` 1.10.8 (so the fallback is the genuine `IntArrays` one), and compared `sortIndirect` against `Arrays.sort` with `comparingInt(i -> keys[i]).thenComparingInt(i -> i)` — the stable signed ascending order the javadoc specifies.

Simulated sections use plane distances of both signs, as `fromDoubleUnaligned` would see them:

```
1. Same keys, either side of RADIX_SORT_THRESHOLD (80)
   quads   path        ordered?  first 4 / last 4 plane distances
   79      quicksort   yes       -15.11 -14.96 -14.94 -14.56  ... +15.02 +15.25 +15.26 +15.48
   80      quicksort   yes       -15.11 -14.96 -14.94 -14.56  ... +15.02 +15.25 +15.26 +15.48
   81      RADIX       NO         +0.58  +0.63  +0.66  +2.24  ...  -2.92  -2.63  -1.07  -0.59
   200     RADIX       NO         +0.58  +0.63  +0.66  +0.87  ...  -0.98  -0.95  -0.92  -0.59

2. Position of the negative-distance quads
   n=80    35 negative quads at positions 0..34 of 0..79   (front - correct)
   n=81    36 negative quads at positions 45..80 of 0..80  (back - WRONG)

3. sortIndirect vs its documented ordering (stable, signed ascending)
   n>80  (radix path)     : 500/500 disagree
   n<=80 (quicksort path) : 0/500 disagree

4. Simulated all-unaligned translucent sections (n = 81..600)
   mis-sorted: 400/400

6. Boundary keys
   MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE/0/+-1 mix (n=200, stable): WRONG
```

Section 6 is worth noting: a plain `Integer.MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`/`0`/`±1` mix also comes out wrong, with no float encoding involved at all — so this is a property of the sort itself, not of how the translucency code uses it.

### Not verified

I have no way to run the game here, so **I have not confirmed any in-game visual artifact**, and I've deliberately not attributed any existing translucency-sorting report to this. The claim is only that the sort disagrees with its own contract and with its own fallback path.

The Java harness and a dependency-free Python reproduction are in the comments on #3925 if they're useful; that PR is closed and should not be merged.

issues.title: GLSL compilation error on Intel iGPU with Vulkan backend: non-opaque uniforms outside a block
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When attempting to run Sodium with Minecraft's experimental Vulkan rendering backend enabled on an integrated Intel Iris X GPU, the game crashes on startup/world load due to a shader compilation error in the block_layer_opaque fragment shader.

### Reproduction Steps

Steps to Reproduce:

Enable the experimental Vulkan rendering pipeline in settings.

Launch the game / load a world with Sodium installed.

The game crashes during frame rendering.

### Log File

[2026-09-12-5.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32150294/2026-09-12-5.log)

### Crash Report

https://mclo.gs/Xwgsres

[Render thread/ERROR]: Couldn't compile FRAGMENT shader sodium:blocks/block_layer_opaque: Couldn't parse GLSL: 0:100: error: 'non-opaque uniforms outside a block' : not allowed when using GLSL for Vulkan
[Render thread/ERROR]: Couldn't compile pipeline sodium:pipeline/solid_terrain: fragment shader sodium:blocks/block_layer_opaque was invalid
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Pipeline is not valid (may contain invalid shaders?)

issues.title: Crash with AbstractBlockRenderContextMixin + MixinTargetAlreadyLoadedException when another mod has its own mixin config
issues.body:
I've been putting together a small client-side mod for NeoForge 1.21.1 and ran into a hard crash on launch as soon as I added my own mixin config (just a second `[[mixins]]` entry in my mods.toml — doesn't touch any Sodium classes at all). With that mod removed, everything boots fine with Sodium mc1.21.1-0.8.13 installed. With it in the mods folder, every single launch crashes with:

`Caused by: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.throwables.MixinTargetAlreadyLoadedException: Critical problem: sodium-neoforge.mixins.json:platform.neoforge.AbstractBlockRenderContextMixin from mod sodium target net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.frapi.render.AbstractBlockRenderContext was loaded too early.
	at org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.MixinInfo.readDeclaredTargets(MixinInfo.java:947)
	at org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.MixinInfo.<init>(MixinInfo.java:881)
	at org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.MixinConfig.prepareMixins(MixinConfig.java:933)
	at org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.MixinConfig.prepare(MixinConfig.java:862)
	at org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.MixinProcessor.prepareConfigs(MixinProcessor.java:540)
	...`

Versions: Sodium mc1.21.1-0.8.13, NeoForge 21.1.250, Minecraft 1.21.1, Java 21.

Steps to reproduce, at least on my machine:

Bare NeoForge 1.21.1 dev environment, drop in Sodium 0.8.13.
Add a second mod with nothing more than a trivial mixin config registered in mods.toml (mine only mixes into vanilla classes, nothing Sodium-related).
Launch. Crashes every time with the trace above.
Remove the second mod's mixin config, keep everything else identical. Boots fine every time.

I dug into it a bit with `-verbose:class` because I was originally trying to hook into Sodium's rendering myself (mixing into `AbstractBlockRenderContext` from my own mod, which is obviously also broken by this same thing). What I saw is that `AbstractBlockRenderContext` gets loaded only about 3-4 seconds into JVM startup, which lines up suspiciously close to NeoForge's early loading screen (`DisplayWindow.updateModuleReads`) doing its first `Class.forName`. My guess — and it's only a guess, I don't know Sodium's or FML's early loading internals well enough to be sure — is that whatever loads `AbstractBlockRenderContext` this early is racing against Mixin's own lazy "prepare all configs on first class transform" step, and the extra time it takes to iterate one more mod's mixin config is sometimes just enough to lose that race.

Not sure if this is fixable on Sodium's side (maybe there's a way to make `AbstractBlockRenderContextMixin` register earlier, or avoid needing that class loaded quite so soon) or if it's really an FML thing, but the crash trace points at Sodium's own mixin so I figured this was the right place to start. Happy to share my full log / a minimal repro mod if that helps track it down.

issues.title: Detect True Bounds of Terrain for Better Frustum Culling
issues.body:
We could detect the true bounding box of terrain within sections to further tighten the frustum test. However, we can't apply this to the frustum test that is performed _within_ occlusion culling because not being able to see the renderable terrain within a section doesn't mean visibility can't propagate to otherwise visible sections behind it. We also can't apply this stricter frustum test to block entities because we don't know their bounds ahead of time so they could render something larger than expected, causing incorrect culling.

Since we perform frustum culling (outside of the frustum-culled occlusion culling pass, which is only used when the camera is stationary) on a bitmap-based section tree that only stores one bit per section, we can't easily store precise section bounds for every section and node in this tree. I think we can probably only implement this type of optimization once we introduce a compute shader for additional section culling.

issues.title: Enhancement: smoother block light for rotated model elements, like NeoForge's new lighting pipeline
issues.body:
This is an enhancement request rather than a bug report. As far as I can tell, Sodium currently matches vanilla behavior in this area. The request is to go beyond vanilla here, the way NeoForge recently did.

### What happens

Blocks whose models are built from rotated elements get one flat block light value per block. A light gradient across several of these blocks turns into a patchwork of visibly stepped tiles instead of a smooth blend. Sky light looks fine, so everything looks normal in daylight. The problem shows up under torches and lanterns at night.

The easiest way to see it is Macaw's Roofs, which is one of the most downloaded decoration mods. Place a patch of any roof blocks near a lantern at night with smooth lighting on. Each roof block renders as its own flat shade. Screenshots are in the first comment below.

### What I ruled out

These are ordinary JSON block models with no custom rendering code involved. In the roofs mod, 53 of 54 block models use rotated elements, which is why the whole roof surface is affected.

The model ambientocclusion flag makes no difference for these faces. I tested that directly with a resource pack that re-enabled ambient occlusion on 225 Macaw's models. The rotated faces did not change at all.

It is not shader related and not a light engine problem. It reproduces with shaders off, and it reproduces identically with Sodium removed, so this is faithful vanilla behavior. The underlying light values are correct: a shader that computes block light per pixel from its own voxel model (Rethinking Voxels) renders the exact same scene perfectly smooth.

### The request

Vanilla treats a quad that is not axis aligned as an inset partial face on its closest axis and hands it a single light value, which is where the flat per-block shading comes from. NeoForge shipped an enhanced lighting pipeline this year that handles these irregular faces properly: it projects the face onto the three axes, computes light for each axis, and blends the results using the components of the face normal. Their write-up explains the whole design and the edge cases they hit: https://neoforged.net/news/enhanced-ao/

Something equivalent in Sodium would fix this for every mod that uses rotated elements, with Macaw's mods alone covering a very large install base. Issue #3227 seems to track a related problem where partial quads get incorrect block light, so there may be shared ground between the two.

### Versions

Minecraft 26.1.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3, Sodium 0.9.1, Macaw's Roofs 2.3.2. Also reproduced on the Sodium 0.8.12 line.

issues.title: ChunkVertexConsumer leaves vertexIndex at 4 when the translucent collector discards a quad
issues.body:
### Version

0.8.13-beta.1 (also present in current `dev`), NeoForge 1.21.1

### What happens

`ChunkVertexConsumer.potentiallyEndVertex` skips the `vertexIndex` reset when the translucent collector discards a quad:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/dev/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/chunk/compile/buffers/ChunkVertexConsumer.java#L136-L140

```java
if (this.material.isTranslucent() && this.collector != null &&
        this.collector.appendQuad(this.vertices, cullFace, normal)) {
   return this;
}
```

`TranslucentGeometryCollector.appendQuad` returns `true` when `TQuad.isInvalid` rejects the quad (more than one duplicated vertex, so a degenerate quad). That early return leaves `vertexIndex` at 4, and the next `addVertex` immediately does `this.vertices[4]`:

```
java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 4 out of bounds for length 4
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.buffers.ChunkVertexConsumer.addVertex(ChunkVertexConsumer.java:42)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer.addVertex(VertexConsumer.java:41)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer.putBulkData(VertexConsumer.java:142)
	at ...mod code emitting quads from AddSectionGeometryEvent...
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.neoforge.level.NeoForgeLevelRenderHooks.runChunkMeshAppenders(NeoForgeLevelRenderHooks.java:35)
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.tasks.ChunkBuilderMeshingTask.execute(ChunkBuilderMeshingTask.java:153)
```

Only geometry pushed through the `VertexConsumer` API hits this, so it shows up for mods rendering into `AddSectionGeometryEvent` (found it in Cable Facades, where facade quads get sliced thin and some come out degenerate). Sodium's own block renderer path is unaffected.

0.6.x did not have this since `appendQuad` returned `void` back then.

### Fix

Reset the index on that path too:

```java
if (this.material.isTranslucent() && this.collector != null &&
        this.collector.appendQuad(this.vertices, cullFace, normal)) {
    this.vertexIndex = 0;
    return this;
}
```

Happy to open a PR if that is useful.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When running Minecraft at 1920×1080 in fullscreen mode with Sodium installed, the GUI Scale setting does not behave correctly.

The available GUI Scale options are 1x, 2x, 3x, and 4x. However, 1x and 2x result in the same effective GUI size, while 3x and 4x also result in the same effective GUI size.

### Reproduction Steps

Launch Minecraft with Sodium installed.
Set the resolution to 1920×1080.
Enable fullscreen mode.
Open the Video Settings and find the GUI Scale setting.
Set GUI Scale to 1x and observe the GUI size.
Change GUI Scale to 2x and compare the GUI size.
Repeat the test with 3x and 4x.
Expected Behavior
Each GUI Scale option should apply a different GUI scaling level when supported by the current resolution.

Actual Behavior
At 1920×1080 fullscreen:

1x and 2x have the same effective GUI scale.
3x and 4x have the same effective GUI scale.
This means that the four GUI Scale options effectively provide only two different GUI sizes.
Environment
Minecraft: 26.2
Sodium: 0.91
Java: 26.2
Resolution: 1920×1080
Display Mode: Fullscreen
GPU: Intel integrated graphics (Core i5-12500H)
Additional Information
The issue occurs when using 1080p fullscreen and appears to affect the GUI Scale setting specifically.

### Log File

The latest.log does not contain any relevant errors or messages related to the GUI Scale issue.

### Crash Report

N/A


Additional Testing

I also tested the issue with the Precise GUI Scalar mod.

With Precise GUI Scalar, I am able to adjust the GUI scale more precisely and get different GUI sizes. However, the GUI becomes blurry / has visible aliasing around text and UI elements when using the non-standard scaling values.

This suggests that the display resolution itself is not preventing the GUI from being scaled. The issue appears to be related specifically to how the standard GUI Scale options are calculated or applied in fullscreen at 1920×1080.

The original issue with Sodium remains:

1x and 2x result in the same effective GUI size.
3x and 4x result in the same effective GUI size.

issues.title: GPU-accelerated entity and block-entity vertex transformation
issues.body:
### Request Description

Minecraft's entity rendering pipeline still performs a significant amount of vertex transformation and buffer preparation on the CPU/render thread. This can become a major bottleneck when rendering large numbers of entities or complex modded entities.

There is an interesting open-source project, [AcceleratedRendering](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/accelerated-rendering), which explores a different approach: caching original meshes and using OpenGL compute shaders to perform vertex transformations in parallel on the GPU before drawing them through the existing rendering pipeline.

I think a similar concept could potentially be integrated into Sodium's renderer architecture.

Potential benefits:

-Reduce CPU/render-thread workload during entity rendering
-Improve performance when rendering large numbers of entities
-Improve performance with complex modded entity models
-Potentially improve block-entity rendering
-Better utilize GPUs when the render thread is CPU-bound
-Potentially provide significant benefits for large modpacks with complex entities

I'm not suggesting directly integrating AcceleratedRendering's implementation, but rather exploring a similar approach that could be designed specifically around Sodium's rendering architecture.

If this is technically feasible, I think it could be an interesting direction to investigate. Thanks for reading!

issues.body:
## Summary

On a dedicated multiplayer server, Sodium's chunk build worker intermittently reads a `PalettedContainer` while the main thread is mutating it, throwing `MissingPaletteEntryException` and killing the client via `emergencySaveAndCrash`.

The underlying race looks transient and harmless — the section is simply mid-update. The fatal part is that `ChunkBuilderMeshingTask` has no recovery path: instead of discarding the result and re-queueing the section for a later frame, the exception propagates through `ChunkJobResult.unwrap` and takes down the game.

## Versions

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 1.21.1 |
| Loader | NeoForge 21.1.235 and 21.1.238 |
| Sodium | **0.8.12** and **0.8.13-beta.2** — both affected |
| Iris | 1.8.14-beta.1 |
| Java | 21.0.7 (Microsoft), 21.0.11 (Azul) |

## Stack trace

```
java.lang.RuntimeException: Exception thrown while executing job
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.executor.ChunkJobResult.unwrap(ChunkJobResult.java:34)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.RenderSectionManager.collectChunkBuildResults(RenderSectionManager.java:532)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.RenderSectionManager.uploadChunks(RenderSectionManager.java:370)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.SodiumWorldRenderer.setupTerrain(SodiumWorldRenderer.java:239)
    at net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.setupRender(LevelRenderer.java:18831)
    ...
Caused by: net.minecraft.world.level.chunk.MissingPaletteEntryException: Missing Palette entry for index 11.
    at net.minecraft.world.level.chunk.LinearPalette.valueFor(LinearPalette.java:76)
    at net.minecraft.world.level.chunk.PalettedContainer.sodium$unpack(PalettedContainer.java:1059)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.world.LevelSlice.unpackBlockData(LevelSlice.java:232)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.world.LevelSlice.copySectionData(LevelSlice.java:197)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.world.LevelSlice.copyData(LevelSlice.java:183)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.pipeline.BlockRenderCache.init(BlockRenderCache.java:50)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.tasks.ChunkBuilderMeshingTask.execute(ChunkBuilderMeshingTask.java:72)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.executor.ChunkJobTyped.execute(ChunkJobTyped.java:49)
    at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.compile.executor.ChunkBuilder$WorkerRunnable.run(ChunkBuilder.java:185)
```

In the final reproductions, the mixin annotations on both `PalettedContainer.sodium$unpack` and `LevelSlice.unpackBlockData` list **only Sodium** — no third-party transformers remain anywhere in the crashing path.

## Reproduction

Multiplayer only (dedicated NeoForge server, ~150 mods, Create-based pack with a high volume of block updates from moving contraptions). Happens while flying or walking through newly loaded terrain. Not reproducible in singleplayer.

Six crashes collected, each with a different palette index:

```
index 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15
```

Across three unrelated machines:

| GPU | Heap | Render distance | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intel Iris Xe | 4 GB | 18 | every few minutes |
| NVIDIA GTX 1660 SUPER | 13 GB | 16 | every 2–5 minutes |
| Intel Iris Xe (laptop) | 16 GB | 16 | occasional |

Client uptime before crash ranged from **99 s to 275 s**.

## What was ruled out

Each of these was removed or disabled, and the crash reproduced afterwards:

| Suspect | How it was eliminated |
|---|---|
| Lithium | Not installed at all on one of the affected clients |
| C2ME 0.3.0+alpha.0.93 | Removed from client; crash persisted |
| ModernFix `perf.compact_bit_storage` | Disabled via `modernfix-mixins.properties`; mixin confirmed gone from the stack (injection offset shifted 1559 → 1059); crash persisted |
| ModernFix (entire mod) | Removed completely, zero occurrences in the crash report; crash persisted |
| Better Biome Reblend | Removed; its `sodium.MixinLevelSlice` confirmed gone from the stack; crash persisted |
| Sodium 0.8.13-beta.2 | Installed; crash persisted |

Downgrading to the 0.6.x branch is **not possible** in this pack: Veil and Sable both declare `sodium >= 0.8.12-alpha.2` as a hard requirement and refuse to load below it.

## Suggested fix

The race itself may be hard to close, but the crash is avoidable. When `ChunkBuilderMeshingTask` hits `MissingPaletteEntryException` — or any exception originating from reading a chunk section that changed underneath it — it could:

1. discard the partial build result,
2. re-queue the render section for rebuild on a later frame.

The worst case then becomes one frame of a stale or missing chunk instead of the client terminating.

Related: #2869

issues.body:
### Bug Description

In the following replay video it is clearly visible that there are _dots_ right on block edges. It is most visible on blocks with darker textures such as black concrete/obsidian (the ones that are shown).
The expectation is for those dots to _not_ appear.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e41b8574-b47c-43af-907b-751ed7368fd2

I should note that this behaviour occurs only when Sodium is enabled and any other mods that I was running during that recording do not affect it. I am also using the NVidia RTX 5060 with the latest drivers installed less than 24h ago right now.

The game version is 1.20.1 and the Sodium version is 0.5.8+mc1.20.1, launched with Prism launcher.

To recreate the bug simply:
- Istall the game version 1.20.1
- Install Sodium (and fabric API)
- Launch the game (I used Prism but I highly doubt that has anything to do with it)
- Place blocks with a darker texture and look at the edges between them (using zoom tools/lowering FOV makes it easier to spot)

[14:20:22] [main/WARN]: Sodium has applied one or more workarounds to prevent crashes or other issues on your system: [AMD_GAME_OPTIMIZATION_BROKEN]
[14:20:22] [main/WARN]: This is not necessarily an issue, but it may result in certain features or optimizations being disabled. You can sometimes fix these issues by upgrading your graphics driver.

And i notice significant performance issues like drop from 200fps to 50fps in certain areas. 

Spark profile: https://spark.lucko.me/WxaEt9DrrV

I reported it to Xaero's World Map and it was said to me that "For some reason an OpenGL operation is very slow for you.". I have the latest 26.7.1 driver and it was installed cleanly with AMD Cleanup utility.

This performance issue did not happen before in the same 1.21.1 version, it happened since i updated my modpack and i tried to revert the Sodium and Iris version but is giving the same results, so maybe it's not completely Sodium related but the message in the latest log worries me, there is something i can do to fix this? issues.title: Crash after refrwshing resource packs with F3+T
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Game randomly crashes when I reload resource packs with F3+T. Not every time, maybe 1 in 3-4 tries, but often enough that it's actually annoying. Sometimes I crash and can just reload again right after and it's fine, sometimes it crashes immediately again

MY guess🤷‍♂️ - F3+T closes the old font atlas texture, and if a sign with text is on screen right at that moment and needs a glyph that isn't baked yet, the game tries to write into a texture that just got freed. Would explain why it's random, it only happens if a sign happens to be rendering at exactly the wrong time

### Reproduction Steps

Refresh with F3+T 1-3 times

issues.title: Video settings crash when page list exceeds window height
issues.body: Reproduced on Minecraft 26.2 with Sodium 0.9.2-alpha.1 on Fabric. Opening Video Settings can pass a negative scrollbar maximum to ScrollbarWidget.setScrollbarContext, causing an IllegalArgumentException from Math.clamp. The affected code clamps total - visible without ensuring the upper bound is non-negative. The current Sodium workaround is to clamp that maximum to zero. A follow-up render can also hit applyButton == null if initialization aborts.

issues.title: Severe 1%/0.1% low FPS on camera rotation at high render distance (occlusion culling not offloaded to async thread)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

### Summary

On Minecraft 26.2 with Sodium 0.9.1, rotating the camera causes large frame-time spikes that are almost invisible in average FPS but devastate the 1% and 0.1% low percentiles. The effect scales steeply with render distance and disappears almost entirely when the camera is held still. Profiling the render thread (spark, wall-clock/async-profiler engine) shows that during camera rotation, self-time in `TraversableTree.traverse` and the surrounding occlusion-culling / render-list / draw-command pipeline increases sharply and *additively* (nothing else decreases to compensate), pointing to this work running synchronously on the render thread instead of being offloaded to the async occlusion-culling thread as documented.

### Environment

- Minecraft version: 26.2
- Sodium version: 0.9.1 (latest for 26.2 at time of testing)
- Mods active during testing: Sodium, Sodium Extra, Sodium Extra Information (all other mods/shaders disabled)
- OS: Linux
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti
- Driver: 610.43.02
- Graphics backend: OpenGL (`preferredGraphicsBackend` set to `"opengl"`; confirmed via profiling — `libnvidia-glcore.so` / `libGLX_nvidia.so` present on the render thread)
- VSync: off
- "Improved Transparency" video setting: off (toggling it on/off has no meaningful effect on the issue)

### Symptom

FPS percentiles measured with the same world/position, varying only render distance and whether the camera is actively rotated:

| Render distance | World | Camera | Avg FPS | 1% low | 0.1% low | Implied 0.1% frame time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | Normal terrain | Rotating | ~400 | 120 | 23 | ~43.5 ms |
| 32 | Normal terrain | Static | ~430 | 240 | 235 | ~4.3 ms |
| 2 | Normal terrain | Rotating | ~1400 | 600 | 350 | ~2.9 ms |
| 2 | Void (empty superflat) | Rotating | ~2000 | 550 | 300 | ~3.3 ms |

Key observations:
- The 0.1% low collapses by ~10x purely from rotating the camera at RD 32, while static-camera performance at the same RD/position is fine.
- The severity scales steeply and non-linearly with render distance (RD 2 → RD 32 is a much larger than 16x increase in worst-case frame time).
- Reproducing in an empty void world (zero blocks, zero entities) still shows the same camera-rotation-triggered pattern, ruling out translucency sorting (water/glass/leaves) as the cause — there is nothing translucent in a void world.
- Disabling the "Improved Transparency" setting does not meaningfully change the behavior, consistent with the above.

### Profiling

Using spark's client profiler (`/sparkc profiler start --interval 1`, async-profiler wall-clock engine) on the **Render thread**, two 10-14s captures were taken at RD 32 in the same location:

- **Control**: camera held completely still.
- **Test**: camera held still for ~2s, then 3 deliberate rapid ~180-360° rotations with short pauses between them.

Comparing aggregated self-time by method (self-time summed across all call-path instances of each method, as a percentage of total captured wall time):

| Method | Control | Test | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.chunk.tree.TraversableTree.traverse` | 0.05% | 1.09% | **+1.04** |
| native `libc.so.6` | 7.39% | 8.43% | +1.03 |
| `jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe.getInt` | 0.00% | 0.71% | +0.71 |
| `RenderSectionManager.tickVisibleRenders` | 0.80% | 1.08% | +0.28 |
| `DefaultChunkRenderer.addSharedIndexedDrawCommands` | 0.00% | 0.28% | +0.28 |
| `ChunkRenderList.add` | 0.00% | 0.25% | +0.25 |
| `org.joml.FrustumIntersection.intersectAab` / `.testAab` | 0.07% | 0.41% | +0.34 |
| `RenderRegion.getStorage` / `.getSectionFlags` | 0.35% | 0.68% | +0.33 |
| `MultiDrawBatch.updateMaxElementCount` / `GL32C.nglMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex` | 0.32% | 0.55% | +0.32 |
| `Tree.deinterleave6` | 0.00% | 0.19% | +0.19 |
| `LocalSectionIndex.pack` | 0.00% | 0.15% | +0.15 |

Total additional self-time attributable to the Sodium chunk-render package: **+2.7 percentage points** in the rotation test vs. the static control. Checking the full delta list, nothing decreases by a comparable amount elsewhere — this is genuinely additive work triggered by rotation, not a redistribution of existing work.

The whole affected set of methods forms a single coherent pipeline: occlusion-culling BFS traversal (`TraversableTree.traverse`) → frustum test (`FrustumIntersection`) → visible-section list rebuild (`RenderSectionManager.tickVisibleRenders`, `ChunkRenderList.add`, `RenderRegion.getStorage/getSectionFlags`) → draw command rebuild/issue (`addSharedIndexedDrawCommands`, `MultiDrawBatch`, `glMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex`).

According to Sodium's own architecture docs, this occlusion-culling traversal is intended to be offloaded to an async thread "when possible" to avoid main-thread stutter. The fact that `TraversableTree.traverse` shows up so prominently *on the render thread itself*, specifically during camera rotation, and specifically scaling with render distance, suggests this case is hitting a synchronous fallback path rather than the async one.

### Notes

- Raw spark profile exports (`.sparkprofile`) for all captures (terrain/void, RD 2/32, control/test) are available on request; happy to upload them to spark's web viewer for interactive flame graphs if useful.
- GPU driver is up to date enough that this doesn't look driver-related (also reproduces identically whether the OpenGL or the default backend is selected).
- This may be related to / a regression alongside the general 26.2 performance reports, but isolating it down to this specific pipeline and trigger (camera rotation at high render distance) seemed worth reporting separately since it's cleanly reproducible and profiled.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Set render distance to 32, disable shaders/other mods, VSync off.
2. Stand still in a normal world; note FPS percentiles are stable (1%/0.1% low close to average).
3. Rapidly rotate the camera (mouse look) for a few seconds; observe 1%/0.1% low percentiles collapse by roughly an order of magnitude relative to average FPS.
4. Repeat in a void/superflat world with no blocks — same pattern persists, ruling out translucency-sorting as the cause.
5. (Optional, to confirm at the code level) Profile the render thread with spark/async-profiler using a short control (static camera) vs. test (repeated rotations) capture at the same render distance, and diff aggregated self-time by method — `TraversableTree.traverse` and the surrounding render-list/draw-command pipeline increase sharply and additively in the rotation case.

issues.title: Mod dependency check fails ("sodium is not installed") for Sodium Extra when "mods" folder is a symlink
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The `mods` folder used for testing is a symbolic link (directory symlink, created via `mklink /D`) pointing to a separate directory on the same disk, rather than being a real/physical directory inside the instance folder. This mirrors a real modpack setup (a git-repo-based modpack where `mods`/`config`/`kubejs` are symlinked into the instance) that worked fine until updating Sodium.

With Sodium 0.8.12 and Sodium Extra 0.9.3 both placed in a **symlinked** `mods` folder, the game fails to start with an FML mod loading crash:

```
-- Mod loading issue for: sodium_extra --
Failure message: Mod sodium_extra requires sodium 0.8.12+mc1.21.1 or above
	Currently, sodium is not installed
Mod version: 0.9.3+mc1.21.1
```

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create an instance where the `mods` directory is a symlink to another directory on disk (e.g. `mklink /D "<instance>\minecraft\mods" "<other path>\mods"`).
2. Place only `sodium-neoforge-0.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar` and `sodium-extra-neoforge-0.9.3+mc1.21.1.jar` in the (symlinked) mods folder.
3. Launch the game.
4. Game crashes on mod loading with: `Mod sodium_extra requires sodium 0.8.12+mc1.21.1 or above. Currently, sodium is not installed`.

- Same two jars (Sodium 0.8.12 + Sodium Extra 0.9.3), same instance, but with `mods` as a **regular (non-symlinked) directory**: game launches successfully, both mods are loaded and present.
- Sodium 0.8.12 alone (no Sodium Extra) in the **symlinked** mods folder: game also launches successfully, and the Mod List log confirms Sodium is loaded (though logged as a "library" file rather than a "mod" file - it does not appear in the in-game Mods menu, but this in itself does not cause a crash).
- Only the combination of (a) symlinked mods folder and (b) another mod (Sodium Extra) declaring a dependency on `sodium` triggers the failure.

### Log File

This log is from my main modpack (not the isolated 2-mod test client), so it includes other mods for context. The mods folder here is also a symlink to a separate directory. issues.title: Entity-format buffers skip the quad encoder since the 26.2 port
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The port to 26.2 swapped `!this.fastFormat` for `!this.blockFormat` in `putBakedQuad`, but those aren't the same check. 26.1's `fastFormat` was true for BLOCK and ENTITY both, while 26.2 gives each its own flag, so what used to mean "neither of these" now means "anything except BLOCK" and every entity-format buffer drops to the vanilla path.

It reads like the rename in went positional, which would explain why the comment on that line still says "check for ENTITY". `!this.blockFormat && !this.entityFormat` gets the old behaviour back. Will open PR fix linked.

issues.title: Screen tearing occurs only when Sodium is installed on Fabric
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When Sodium is installed on Fabric, the game consistently exhibits screen tearing that does not occur in vanilla Minecraft.

With VSync enabled, FPS is correctly limited to 60, but a slow-moving horizontal tear line remains visible while rotating the camera. With VSync disabled, normal tearing occurs.

The issue is reproducible in a completely clean Fabric instance containing only:
- Fabric Loader
- Fabric API
- Sodium

Removing Sodium from the exact same instance immediately eliminates the tearing.

I have reproduced this on multiple Sodium versions and on Minecraft 1.20.1 and 1.21.x.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create a fresh Fabric instance.
2. Install only Fabric API and Sodium.
3. Launch the game.
4. Enable VSync.
5. Enter any world.
6. Rotate the camera horizontally.

Expected:
No visible screen tearing, matching vanilla Minecraft.

Actual:
A slow-moving horizontal tear line is visible across the screen. Removing Sodium from the same instance immediately eliminates the issue.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Environment:

OS: macOS 26.2 (aarch64 / Apple Silicon, M2 Pro)
Java: 21.0.11 (Azul Zulu)
Minecraft: 1.21.1
Loader: NeoForge 21.1.238
Launcher: Modrinth App (Theseus)

Game crashes consistently during initial screen setup with:
java.lang.RuntimeException: Sodium mod config not found
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.config.ConfigManager.registerConfigs(ConfigManager.java:119)
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.config.ConfigManager.registerConfigsLate(ConfigManager.java:76)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.handler$xxx$sodium$postInit(Minecraft.java)
	at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.buildInitialScreens(Minecraft.java:675)

Steps taken to isolate (all failed to resolve the crash):

Removed/disabled Dynamic Surroundings (dsurround) — no change
Removed/disabled Iris — caused a different crash (Veil NPE due to missing Iris dependency), confirming Iris is required by Veil
Removed/disabled Sable and Veil together — crash persisted identically, ruling them out
Deleted and let regenerate sodium-options.json — crash persisted
Fully redownloaded Sodium jar via Modrinth (fresh copy, not cached) — crash persisted
Downgraded Sodium to 0.8.12-beta.2 — identical crash, different jar hash
Confirmed only one Sodium jar exists in mods folder (no duplicates)
Disabled all other config-library mods simultaneously (Cloth Config, Fzzy Config, YetAnotherConfigLib, SuperMartijn642's Config Library) — crash persisted
Disabled Forgified Fabric API — crash persisted (though it may still be present via jar-in-jar from dependent mods)

The crash occurs at the exact same point (registerConfigsLate) regardless of which other mods are present, suggesting this may not be a mod-conflict issue but something specific to how Sodium reads its own bundled default-config resource in this environment (possibly macOS ARM/Apple Silicon-specific, since that's the one constant across all tests).

### Reproduction Steps

Sodium versions tested: 0.8.12+mc1.21.1, 0.8.12-beta.2+mc1.21.1 (both fail identically)
~140 mod modpack including Iris, Veil, Sable, Create, and various Fabric-API-shimmed mods via Forgified Fabric API

issues.body:
# Bug Report: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION in CommandEncoder.writeToBuffer on Snapdragon X Elite (Windows-on-ARM)

## Summary

Minecraft crashes reliably during normal gameplay with a native JVM crash (`EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION`) inside `com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.CommandEncoder.writeToBuffer`, while Sodium is active. The crash occurs on Windows-on-ARM64 hardware with a Qualcomm Adreno GPU. This happens with Sodium alone (no Iris/shaders installed), and is not resolved by switching to an x64 (emulated) Java runtime instead of native ARM64 Java — indicating the fault lies in the interaction between Sodium's rendering path and the Adreno OpenGL driver itself, not in Java/JVM architecture.

## System Information

- **Device**: Snapdragon X Elite (X1E80100), Qualcomm Oryon CPU, 12 cores, 16GB RAM
- **OS**: Windows 11, 64-bit, Build 26100 (10.0.26100.8115) — Windows-on-ARM
- **GPU**: Qualcomm Adreno (integrated), using driver files under `qcdx8380.inf_arm64`
- **Minecraft version**: 1.21.2 (assetIndex 32)
- **Mod loader**: Fabric Loader 0.19.3-26.2
- **Mods installed at time of crash**: Sodium (latest available), Sodium mixin core visible in crash (`net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.mixin.core.CommandEncoderAccessor`). Iris was **not** installed for the most recent reproduction.
- **Java runtime tested**:
  - Native ARM64 OpenJDK 25 (bundled Minecraft runtime, windows-aarch64) — crashes
  - x64 (emulated via Windows Prism) Zulu OpenJDK 21.0.11 — same crash still occurs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Minecraft 1.21.2 via Fabric Loader 0.19.3-26.2 with Sodium installed.
2. Play normally (no shaders required — reproduced both with and without Iris installed).
3. After roughly 40–90 seconds of gameplay, the game crashes with a native JVM fatal error.

## Crash Details

Both crash logs point to the same faulting method and object types:

```
EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005)
Problematic frame: C  0x... (no source info available)

Current thread: "Render thread" [_thread_in_Java]

X12 = {method} 'writeToBuffer'
      '(Lcom/mojang/blaze3d/buffers/GpuBufferSlice;Ljava/nio/ByteBuffer;)V'
      in 'com/mojang/blaze3d/systems/CommandEncoder'
```

Relevant objects on the stack at crash time:
- `com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlBuffer$Direct` (size 1280, usage 136, canPersistentMap=true)
- `com.mojang.blaze3d.buffers.Std140Builder`
- `java.nio.DirectByteBuffer` (capacity 32)
- `com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.DirectStateAccess$Emulated`

The generic signature on `CommandEncoder` explicitly shows Sodium's mixin hook:
```
Ljava/lang/Object;Lnet/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/mixin/core/CommandEncoderAccessor;
```

This confirms Sodium's `CommandEncoderAccessor` mixin is involved in the code path at the point of the crash.

## Reproducibility / Isolation Steps Already Taken

- ✅ Reproduced with Iris **removed** — rules out Iris/shader-specific code as the sole cause.
- ✅ Reproduced with **x64 (Prism-emulated) Java** instead of native ARM64 Java — rules out ARM64 JIT compilation or ARM64-specific JVM bugs as the cause.
- ✅ Confirmed x64 Java itself runs correctly on this system (`java -version` succeeds) — the crash is not a general "Java doesn't run" issue.
- Two separate crash logs captured ~24 minutes apart, both faulting at the identical method with the identical object types and Sodium mixin class involved, suggesting a consistent, reproducible fault rather than a one-off memory corruption event.

## Suspected Cause

Given that:
1. The crash is isolated to `CommandEncoder.writeToBuffer`, specifically a Sodium-mixed-in code path,
2. It reproduces independent of Java architecture (ARM64 native vs. x64 emulated),
3. It reproduces without Iris/shaders,

...the most likely explanation is an incompatibility between Sodium's GPU buffer-writing code path and the Adreno OpenGL driver's handling of persistent-mapped buffers or DirectByteBuffer writes on Windows-on-ARM. Sodium's own documentation notes that Windows-on-ARM devices using OpenGL translation layers are not officially supported and "will have severe performance issues" — this may be a related or overlapping issue where the interaction goes beyond performance into an outright native crash.

## Attachments

Two full `hs_err_pid*.log` crash logs are available and can be provided if needed (not attached here for brevity — happy to paste full logs or upload on request).

## Environment Notes

This is a fairly new class of hardware (Snapdragon X Elite Windows-on-ARM laptops), and ARM64/Adreno driver support across the Minecraft modding ecosystem may still be maturing. Filing this in case it's useful data for prioritizing ARM64/Adreno compatibility work, or in case others with similar hardware are hitting the same issue.

issues.title: Lag issues related to signs worsened between Minecraft versions 1.21.8 and 1.21.11
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The issue of signs causing significant lag has long been known; however, most reports originated from test worlds where signs were excessively densely packed, and there was little noticeable impact during usual gameplay worlds.

However, as soon as I upgraded my usual gameplay world from version 1.21.8 to 1.21.11, severe lag occurred—so intense that it significantly hindered gameplay.

The situation worsened further in version 26.2; the frame rate would drop to single digits with just seven or eight glowing signs in view. Disabling the sign glow makes things somewhat better, but it remains sluggish—far from the smooth performance of version 1.21.8.

I normally use Sodium; while it previously worked well to optimize sign rendering, it appears that this optimization is no longer functioning effectively as of version 1.21.11. There is a possibility that this is a bug in Sodium rather than Minecraft itself, so I report it here.

I wanted to upload videos capturing the issue, but the upload kept failing for some reason, so I am providing links to Google Drive instead:

Correct behavior in MC 1.21.8:

issues.title: Checkerboard-pattern invisible (sky-colored) chunks above Y64, occurs even when stationary
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Certain chunks become fully sky-colored (as if unrendered / occluded) at Y=64 and above, in a distinct checkerboard pattern — every other chunk is affected, alternating with normal chunks. This is not a single random chunk going invisible; it's a consistent alternating pattern.

This happens both while moving and while completely stationary — it is not related to chunk loading/streaming lag. Running `F3+A` (rebuild chunks) always fixes it immediately, until it reoccurs later during the session.

I expect chunks at any Y level to render normally without needing to manually force a chunk rebuild.

Additional findings that rule out other causes:
- Reproduces on multiple unrelated servers, including vanilla Paper servers with no plugins installed, ruling out server-side causes.
- Reproduces across different Sodium versions, including both beta and stable/release builds — not a beta-specific regression.
- Reproduces regardless of installed mods or mod combination, ruling out mod interaction as the cause.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Join a world/server (reproduces on both vanilla Paper servers and other third-party servers).
2. Move to or above Y=64 (sea level).
3. Observe that some chunks render normally while neighboring chunks (in an alternating/checkerboard pattern) render as solid sky color instead of terrain.
4. This can occur even while standing completely still, with no camera movement.
5. Press F3+A to force a chunk rebuild — the affected chunks render correctly again.
6. After some time/movement, the issue reoccurs in the same or different chunks.

### Log File

I cannot find anything unusual.

### Crash Report

I cannot find anything unusual.

issues.title: Fantastic Wings (Fabric) renders Avian Wings without feathers
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Hello!

I found a rendering issue that appears to be specific to Sodium on Fabric.

**Environment:**
- Minecraft 1.20.1
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3
- Fabric API 0.92.9
- Pizzle Lib 8.1.33
- Sodium 0.5.13
- Fantastic Wings v20.1.1
- orge Config Api Port 8.0.3

**Issue:**
When Sodium is installed, Avian Wings from Fantastic Wings render without feathers. Only the skeletal wing model is displayed.

Without Sodium, the wings render correctly with full feather geometry.

**Troubleshooting performed:**
- Tested Sodium 0.5.8 → Same issue
- Installed Indium → No change
- Installed Iris → No change
- Installed Sodium Extra → No change
- Disabled Sodium rendering options (Entity Culling, Block Face Culling, etc.) → No change

**Comparison:**
I tested the exact same version of Fantastic Wings on NeoForge using Embeddium.

**Results:**
✔ NeoForge + Embeddium → Wings render correctly
✘ Fabric + Sodium → Feather geometry missing

This makes me think the issue is specific to Sodium's Fabric renderer, since Embeddium does not exhibit the same behavior.

### Reproduction Steps

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Launch Minecraft 1.20.1 with these mods installed:
   - Fabric Loader 0.19.3
   - Fabric API 0.92.9
   - Pizzle Lib 8.1.33
   - Sodium 0.5.13
   - Fantastic Wings v20.1.1
   - Forge Config Api Port 8.0.3

2. Create or load a single-player world (Creative mode recommended).

3. Open the Creative inventory and search for **"Angel Wings Bottle"** and add the item that does **not** have "Splash" or "Lingering" in its name to your inventory.  
   *(Alternatively, you can use the command: `/wings give @p angel_wings`)*  
   > **Note:** You can also try these variants instead of "Angel": Parrot, Fire, Bat, Evil, Dragon, and Metallic.

4. Drink the potion (skip this step if you used the command).

5. Press **F5** to switch to third-person view and observe the equipped wings on your character.

6. **Actual result:** The wings appear as a bare skeleton frame — all feather layers are missing.

7. **(For comparison)** Quit the game, remove Sodium from the mods folder (keeping all other mods), and repeat steps 2–5.

issues.title: Add macOS fullscreen mode option with configurable render scaling (F11 fullscreen behavior)

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

issues.body:
### Request Description

### Problem
On macOS, Minecraft fullscreen behavior differs depending on how fullscreen is triggered:

* Using Fn + F (or macOS native fullscreen behavior):

    * The game enters macOS fullscreen (Spaces / separate desktop)
    * This allows smooth switching between desktops (browser, Discord, etc.)
    * macOS display resolution remains unchanged
    * However, Minecraft still renders at full Retina resolution
    * On high-resolution displays this leads to unnecessary GPU load and reduced performance, especially with shaders
* Using F11 (Minecraft fullscreen toggle):
    * enters either borderless or exclusive fullscreen depending on the current configuration
    * typically uses a fixed resolution (e.g. 1920×1200 on many macOS setups - is applied for the whole macOS system, like mouse pointer, other windows from other applications etc. which leads to problems when using other apps while Minecraft is in such a fullscreen mode)
    * does not behave like macOS native fullscreen (Spaces)

### Feature to solve this problem

**Add a macOS-specific fullscreen rendering option**, located in the Minecraft settings under full screen mode

### 1. Fn + F behavior (unchanged)

* No changes to current behavior
* Game enters fullscreen normally - macOS native fullscreen
* Rendering remains at full native resolution
* Works exactly as it does today with any macOS application

### **2. F11 behavior (new option - located in Minecraft settings unter full screen mode, where you can already choose between borderless/exclusive)**

When pressing F11:

* Minecraft enters macOS native fullscreen mode instead of borderless mode or exclusive mode (Spaces / separate desktop - like when clicking full screen on a YouTube Video and it opens in macOS native fullscreen mode)
    * Same system behavior as other macOS fullscreen applications
    * Allows smooth switching between desktops (browser, Discord, etc.)
    * macOS display resolution/display scaling remains unchanged
* Additionally:
    * Apply a configurable render scaling factor → can be configured in the Minecraft graphics settings
        * e.g. 50%, 75%, 100%
    * This scales only Minecraft rendering
        * reduces internal render resolution
        * improves performance (especially with shaders and high DPI displays)

issues.title: Parallelization of Occlusion Culling
issues.body: ### Request Description Basically i noticed that the single threaded BFS is inefficient and causing frametime spikes on aysnc cull thread which i noticed when i was profiling minecraft ( dev stream current ) using jfr . i saw that the highest cpu time used class was OcclusionCuller. So what i ask/propose is that we Parallelize the BFS traversal(ik BFS and parallelization together sounds crazy but its possible just hard ) using layer by layer batching or using suggestions of your choice , I was wondering if it would be what Sodium is moving forwards or is this change not planned ? I am already working on an implementation locally and so far only 1 bug is left to fix , I would love to work on an implementation with other contributors/maintainers and increase my knowledge. The issue I am basically facing is that Layer by layer BFS is already done and working but only when player is moving , there is some z-fighting issue too but I am working on a way to fix these issues would love feedback i can produce a Pr and Draft it Tomorrow so that you can see my code and we can collaborate .

issues.title: Proposed optimization: Parallelize batch building across regions on worker threads
issues.body:
### Request Description

Right Now , fillCommandBuffer() runs on the render thread and rebuilds command buffers for every region every time the camera crosses a section boundary. The face culling + native memory writes are pure math with no API dependencies so  they should be able to run in parallel on worker threads.
So Basically what i propose is that each region's MultiDrawBatch gets built on a worker thread. The render thread only does the serialized multiDrawIndexed() submission. This would scale ~4x on common CPUs with no OpenGL/Vulkan divergence.
Two questions before I open a Draft PR :
1.Is there a thread-safety concern I'm missing with the MultiDrawBatch.size field?
2.Would you prefer a bounded thread pool or the existing chunk build workers for this?

I expect about 5-15% fps improvements and about 2ms shaven off the render thread on Cpu limited situations,  high render distance, low-end Cpu basically. Not huge but ,the batch building time varies per frame  ,  when the camera crosses a section boundary, all regions invalidate at once, creating a 4ms spike of batch building. ,That's a micro stutter. Making it parallel smooths that spike to 1ms. I think this more valuable than the average FPS gain.

Please provide feedback 
Btw made an issue because didn't feel like doing a large change and submitting a PR without checking with maintainers/contributors isn't right.

issues.title: NullPointerException in TopoGraphSorting.topoGraphSort ("allQuads" is null) on chunk build, persists with terrain_sorting_enabled set to false
issues.body:
### Bug Description

### Bug Description

Repeated `NullPointerException: Cannot read the array length because "allQuads" is null` 
in `TopoGraphSorting.topoGraphSort`, thrown from a chunk builder worker thread and 
propagating up through `ChunkJobResult.unwrap` to crash the game on the render thread.

This has now occurred across multiple distinct triggers, all of which involve a large/sudden 
batch of chunk (re)builds rather than any single specific block or location:

- Loading into a singleplayer world (cold start)
- Standing near dense sculk sensor/shrieker clusters
- Increasing render distance from 12 to 24 while in-world
- With shaders (Iris + Mellow) fully disabled — ruling out shader interaction
- With Distant Horizons disabled — ruling out LOD-related rebuild triggers
- With `fullbright`/gamma overrides — unrelated, just visibility, not causation

I also tried setting `terrain_sorting_enabled: false` directly in `sodium-options.json` 
(confirmed via Sodium options that this is what's officially called "Translucent Face Sorting" 
and gates the dynamic/topological sort path). The value persists as `false` across restarts 
and is not being reverted by any other mod. **The crash still occurs through the exact same 
gated code path even with this set to false.** This suggests either the option doesn't fully 
gate `DynamicTopoSorter`/`TopoGraphSorting`, or there's a second code path (possibly already-
queued jobs from before the setting change, or a section state that bypasses the check) that 
still reaches it.

### Reproduction Steps

issues.title: DefaultChunkRenderer desyncs `GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram` if no draw calls are made, causing the player's hand to disappear in specific cases
issues.body: ### Bug Description It's a bit hard to explain, please bear with me. The way `DefaultChunkRenderer.render()` is written can cause Mojang's `GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram` cache to desync, which makes the game incorrectly skip binding a later program, which typically manifests itself as the player's first-person hand disappearing. `DefaultChunkRenderer.render()` does: ```java try (RenderPass pass = encoder.createRenderPass(...)) { pass.setPipeline(this.activeProgram); drawContext.setContext(pass, this.activeProgram); // basically just a raw GL33C.glUseProgram call ... while (iterator.hasNext()) { ... if (batch.isEmpty()) continue; // every batch can be skipped batch.draw(drawContext); // <-- the only place that updates GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram } } ``` `batch.draw()` eventually reaches the vanilla path that updates `GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram`, but `GLDrawContext.setContext()` alone doesn't update it and `batch.draw()` can be completely skipped if all batches are empty. So when there is nothing to draw, `GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram` becomes stale. The next time vanilla submits a draw using the pipeline that the game thinks is still bound, it skips the rebind. But the real GL program is Sodium's terrain shader. The vanilla geometry gets rendered with the wrong shader and, in the cases I've observed so far, it effectively disappears. Expected behavior: In user-facing terms, I would expect to not have weird edge cases where my hand disappears. In code terms, I would expect either: - `DefaultChunkRenderer.render()` to return early before calling `GLDrawContext.setContext()` if there is nothing to draw, or - `GLDrawContext.setContext()` to invalidate/update Mojang's `GlCommandEncoder.lastProgram` cache instead of silently desyncing it. ### Reproduction Steps 1. In Minecraft 26.2 with Sodium 0.9.0, create a test world with: - superflat type - structures disabled - gamerules spawn_mobs, advance_time, advance_weather disabled 2. In video settings, turn off clouds. Leave the rest at defaults. ("Improved transparency" must remain off.) 3. Run command: `/summon allay ~ ~ ~ {NoAI:1b}` 4. Move a bit so you can see the allay. Stay in first-person mode. 5. Watch your hand disappear when you're looking directly at the allay and reappear when you're looking away. Why superflat with no structures, no mobs, no weather, no clouds? The translucent layer needs to be completely empty (no water, glass, slimes, rain, clouds), otherwise you won't see the bug. Why no advance_time? Just for convenience. Why no "Improved transparency"? The translucent layer works differently with that setting enabled. Haven't looked into it in detail, but basically the bug doesn't happen with that setting. Why an allay? I was looking for a mob with translucent features and allay came up first because of the name. A slime would probably work too. ### Log File [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29149105/latest.log) ### Crash Report [crash-2026-06-19_21.44.29-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29149131/crash-2026-06-19_21.44.29-client.txt)

issues.title: Sodium fails to restore modifications to PEB in newer NeoForge versions
issues.body: ### Bug Description (I originally reported this on Discord and was asked to also open an issue here) Hi, I am on the development team of an overlay app for Minecraft. When running Sodium on NeoForge for Mc1.21.10+ the game process's command-line is being overwritten to "net.caffeinemc.sodium / net.minecraft.client.main.Main /" as part of your Nvidia / AMD workaround, but isn't restored. This is a critical problem for our overlay app, because we need to read that command-line string to detect the game's info, such as game directory, mcVersion, launcher, etc. Currently our only solution is to show a "Sodium mod conflict - app disabled" message to users when the problem occurs... And unsurprisingly, many of our users are also running Sodium, so this problem is quite prevalent. Here's what @jellysquid3 said about this on Discord: > Sodium is supposed to restore the modifications to PEB after it has initialized the OpenGL context Since the drivers don't check after that point I'd guess the problem is actually that on newer NeoForge versions, we don't restore them properly There are some known bugs with it right now, due to how the early window initialization works on NeoForge: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3664 Might be related. According to our tests, the command-line remains properly readable on older NeoForge versions (before Mc1.21.10) and on all Fabric versions, so this seems to be a relatively new issue that only occurs with newer NeoForge versions. I tested the PR https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/pull/3697 but it seems to be unrelated and didn't solve the issue. ### Reproduction Steps 1. issues.title: Problems with mcmeta files

labels.name: B-LTS
labels.description: Branch: Only relevant for LTS, unapplicable on current

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Animated experience_bottle.png textures do not animate when Sodium is installed.
The texture should animate normally using a standard .png.mcmeta animation file.
When Sodium is installed, the animation is not played and the item appears static. The same resource pack works correctly without Sodium

### Reproduction Steps

Create a resource pack containing:
assets/minecraft/textures/item/experience_bottle.png (16x32 texture with 2 animation frames)
assets/minecraft/textures/item/experience_bottle.png.mcmeta
Use the following mcmeta file:
{
  "animation": {
    "frametime": 15,
    "interpolate": true
  }
}
Launch Minecraft without Sodium and observe that the texture animates.
Install Sodium and launch the game again.
Observe that the animation no longer plays.

### Log File

It doesn't crash, only the animation doesn't play

### Crash Report

 doesn't crash

issues.title: Crash with Latest Supplementaries Version when Loading Worlds
issues.body:
### Bug Description

(NeoForge 1.21.1-3.6.7) (sodium-neoforge-0.8.12-beta.1+mc1.21.1)
After updating my modpack I noticed it was crashing when I went to open a world. After narrowing it down, I found that Supplementaries and Sodium are in conflict when both are on their most recent versions.

### Reproduction Steps

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the most recent versions of Sodium, Supplementaries, and the dependency Moonlight Lib
2. Open any world
3. Game will crash

### Log File

https://mclo.gs/0pMSzvc

### Crash Report

https://mclo.gs/6NNiRGi

issues.title: Out of Memory Crashes in Combination With Skyblock-related Mods
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Two users are experiencing out of memory-related crashes (various stack traces) when running the game for many hours in combination with skyblock mods. It's so far unclear whether sodium is necessary and/or involved in the underlying issue. We've so far received no confirmation of this issue without some collection of skyblock-related mods.

One user tried removing individual skyblock mods and couldn't get it to not crash and didn't experience the crashes on a separate non-skyblock instance, so a hardware or OS issue seems unlikely unless it is specifically aggravated by these skyblock mods.

Spark: https://spark.lucko.me/ln2f6nTLbU (nothing interesting as far as I can see)

I also analyzed a full heap dump from this user, and could not find anything problematic.

issues.title: Use GL_REPEAT instead of GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE for blocks atlas texture edge extensions

labels.name: F-good-first-issue
labels.description: Flag: Good first issue for new contributors

issues.body: ### Request Description Screenshot from the Vibrant Visuals channel on the feedback server: It may be worth changing (or adding an option to change) the texture extension method used for blocks to repeat the edges in mirrored form, rather than repeating only the border pixels outward. For example the texture abcd would be padded as dcbaabcddcba rather than aaaaabcddddd. This would result in an overall cleaner mipmapping experience in cases like the one depicted. Also relevant could be an option to switch off texture padding entirely, as vanilla does not allow you to do this; this would reduce the amount of memory taken up by atlases (since due to #3690 non-power-of-two sized texture files do not tessellate well) but may occasionally result in thin artifacts at the edges of some textures.

issues.title: Reduce graphical memory usage by packing atlases more efficiently

labels.name: F-good-first-issue
labels.description: Flag: Good first issue for new contributors

issues.body: ### Request Description Let's use F3+S to dump all the atlases: If we open this and examine it, looking at some of the power-of-two boundaries starting from the top left will reveal whole avenues of unoccupied space going down and across the whole atlas. This space could easily have been filled in by other sprites, but it ultimately is not: it seems that once a whole 2^a*2^b space is exhausted, the game starts filling in from a starting point outside of there without accounting for the unused space in the previous area. This could result in atlas dimensions which are bigger than they need to be, ultimately consuming more graphical memory. There must be a more intelligent way to populate atlases with sprites in a way that does not result in these wide gaps manifesting, which would improve performance due to the decrease in graphical memory required for a smaller atlas.

issues.title: [26.1] Breaks custom water tint registered in Fabric's `FluidRenderingRegistry`
issues.body: ### Bug Description Hey, a client-side [mod](https://modrinth.com/mod/natural-waters) of mine changes the water color. Sodium breaks that, and always shows the vanilla color. I'm not using any Mixins, only mod loader provided APIs. I would expect those to remain fully functional, even when Sodium is installed. https://github.com/Fuzss/natural-waters/blob/26.1.x/Fabric/src/main/java/fuzs/naturalwaters/fabric/client/NaturalWatersFabricClient.java After looking into this I found that in general when overriding water rendering via Fabric's `FluidRenderingRegistry` the color provided by the set `BlockTintSource` is not respected when Sodium is installed. ### Reproduction Steps Here are some very simple steps to reproduce the issue: ```java FluidModel.Unbaked WATER_MODEL = new FluidModel.Unbaked(FluidStateModelSet.WATER_MODEL.stillMaterial(), FluidStateModelSet.WATER_MODEL.flowingMaterial(), FluidStateModelSet.WATER_MODEL.overlayMaterial(), state -> -1); FluidRenderingRegistry.register(Fluids.WATER, Fluids.FLOWING_WATER, WATER_MODEL); ``` All this does is render the water texture as it is, which makes it render white. With only Fabric that works fine. When Sodium is installed the custom color is ignored and the vanilla color is used. (Note that the cauldron water color is replaced separately, it's mainly here to test that the `BlockTintSource` is working correctly.) ### Log File https://mclo.gs/OBM13cb ### Crash Report Can't generate one, the key combination does not seem to work on Mac OS.
