issues.title: Driver workarounds are applied twice when FML early window control is disabled
issues.body:
### Bug Description

On NeoForge, when early window control is disabled, driver workarounds are applied twice, potentially causing error.

The first, in `GraphicsBootstrapper`:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/59e7586b49da6ba278912d03e8d83eef7a8b07d5/neoforge/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/service/SodiumWorkarounds.java#L23-L24

The second, in `WindowMixin`:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/59e7586b49da6ba278912d03e8d83eef7a8b07d5/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/mixin/workarounds/context_creation/WindowMixin.java#L40-L41

The root cause seems to be a change in NeoForge. On 1.21.1 the `glfwCreateWindow` call is [removed](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/869777fa2e6fc91b55a406e4b9733cb1dca92402/patches/com/mojang/blaze3d/platform/Window.java.patch#L7-L9), so the `WindowMixin` won't inject. On 1.21.11+, however, the `glfwCreateWindow` call [remains](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/6cb49467014c294e6cd6adae618d516a27c17cb5/patches/com/mojang/blaze3d/platform/Window.java.patch#L11) in place.

Note: This had been reported in https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3636 but it was wrongly attributed to Ixeris or Async Logger.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create a 1.21.11+ NeoForge instance and launch, for `fml.toml` to be created
2. In `fml.toml`, set `earlyWindowControl = false`
3. Install Sodium and launch the game
4. Observe that the driver workarounds are applied twice (the game might crash with message "Command line is already modified")

### Log File

Not needed (something similiar to "Modifying process environment to apply workarounds for the AMD graphics driver..." would be printed twice)

### Crash Report

See #3636

issues.title: ClassNotFoundException: net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.gui.SodiumGameOptions when Sable mixin accesses Sodium internals
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The game crashes during initialization with a Mixin transformer error. The crash occurs when Sable’s mixin sable.mixins.json:sublevel_render.impl.sodium.SodiumWorldRendererMixin attempts to access the field performance of the class net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.gui.SodiumGameOptions. However, this class does not exist in the installed version of Sodium, leading to a ClassNotFoundException.

Environment:

Minecraft: 1.21.1

NeoForge: 21.1.228

Sodium: net.caffeinemc.sodium-neoforge-0.8.12-alpha.1+mc1.21.1-mod.jar (alpha version)

Sable: sable-neoforge-1.21.1-1.2.2.jar

Also present: Sinytra Connector 2.0.0-beta.14, Iris (disabled via config), many Create addons.

Crash stack trace (relevant part):

text
java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.gui.SodiumGameOptions
	at ... 
Caused by: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.throwables.MixinPreProcessorException: Attach error for sable.mixins.json:sublevel_render.impl.sodium.SodiumWorldRendererMixin from mod sable during activity: [Transform -> Method sable$setupTerrain(...) -> GETFIELD -> net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/gui/SodiumGameOptions::performance:Lnet/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/gui/SodiumGameOptions$PerformanceSettings;]
Expected behavior:
Sable should either not rely on internal Sodium GUI classes that may change between versions, or it should check for the existence of such classes before attempting to access them. Using stable public APIs or reflection with fallback would be more robust.

Additional notes:

The crash disappears when Sable is removed from the mods folder. 

The same error occurs with or without Iris (Iris was disabled).

Sodium version is an alpha; maybe Sable expects a different package structure (e.g., me.jellysquid.mods.sodium vs net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium). The class SodiumGameOptions appears to have been moved or renamed in recent Sodium builds.

### Reproduction Steps

Prerequisites:

Minecraft: 1.21.1

NeoForge: 21.1.228

Java: Microsoft OpenJDK 21.0.7 (or any Java 21)

Required mods (minimum):

Sodium: net.caffeinemc.sodium-neoforge-0.8.12-alpha.1+mc1.21.1 (the alpha version is crucial)

Sable: sable-neoforge-1.21.1-1.2.2

Steps:

Install NeoForge 1.21.1.

Place both .jar files into the mods folder.

Launch the game.

Observed crash:

The game crashes during initialization with:

text
java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.gui.SodiumGameOptions
The stack trace points to Sable's mixin:
sable.mixins.json:sublevel_render.impl.sodium.SodiumWorldRendererMixin
attempting to access the field SodiumGameOptions.performance.

Expected behavior:

The game should load successfully, or Sable should gracefully handle the missing class (e.g., disable the feature).

Additional notes:

The crash does not occur if Sable is removed.

The crash does not occur with a stable (non‑alpha) version of Sodium . The internal class SodiumGameOptions appears to have been moved or renamed in the alpha build.

Full error snippet from the log:
Caused by: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.throwables.MixinPreProcessorException: Attach error for sable.mixins.json:sublevel_render.impl.sodium.SodiumWorldRendererMixin from mod sable during activity: [Transform -> Method sable$setupTerrain(...) -> GETFIELD -> net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/gui/SodiumGameOptions::performance:Lnet/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/gui/SodiumGameOptions$PerformanceSettings;]

issues.title: Translucent texture leads to rendering quirks only on 26.1 and above
issues.body:
### Bug Description

In the NewDefault+ texture pack, leaf textures have translucent sections (opacity 1/255) to make them look better for people using fast graphics/non-see-through leaves. This used to work fine for vanilla and sodium up to 1.21.11. Since 26.1, these translucent textures work fine in vanilla but will cause some slight problems with sodium.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd6ad8af-3c74-4585-87c1-796228a3bda9

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de61b7b7-7a88-4625-ad72-b5800e4be4a6

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b9fea20-0efa-47f6-85d9-9d87bb0daa37

Some issues with translucent textures on 26.1+
- incorrectly occluded vanilla clouds
- a weird "foggy"/seethrough-ish effect
- waving textures not working with shaders

### Reproduction Steps

- Install Sodium, Iris, and some shaders (Complementary Unbound, Red Hat, and Steadfast in my case) into versions 1.20.11 and 26.1
- Download the NewDefault+ texture pack (v1.82 as of writing) and apply
- Without shaders, position the camera so that the bushy part of the leaves collide with a cloud and notice the cloud cutout that only happens on 26.1 (this does not happen in vanilla but a workaround in sodium is turning on improved transparency)
- Apply shaders, and notice how tree leaves look "foggy" inside, can be somewhat see-through, and do not wave, only on 26.1

issues.title: Support Rendering Unsorted Translucent Quads
issues.body:
Some mods, such as BBE, generate translucent quads that should not be sorted. The sorting system can handle them, but it's an unnecessary overhead and sometimes it breaks in ways that cause incorrect rendering, especially on Safe quad splitting mode.

The ideal solution to this would be to mesh them into a separate buffer that is prepended to the rest of the translucent quads and then a monotonous prefix is written into the index buffer. This requires some plumbing in the mesh buffer handling, the translucent quad collector, and the `Sorter`s for offsetting the quad indices of the regularly sorted quads.

To mark quads as being translucent but requiring no sorting, some changes to the meshing process are required and a parameter should be introduced that lets mods indicate that they want this special path to be taken.

issues.title: Sodium causes total amdGPU device crash at random on Linux
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The game crashes randomly when playing with sodium on. The crash causes a total failure of the GPU, resulting in the kernel needing to reset the device to continue function. In journalctl, the errors listed are page fault, GCVM L2 protection fault, faulty UTCL 2 client, Walker error 0, permission fault and mapping error. This only seems to happen in any fullscreen mode.

### Reproduction Steps

Step 1: ensure you have amdgpu and game set to fullscreen (this seems to trigger the issue)
Step 2: play game until it freezes. This can happen immediately or after some time

### Log File

issues.title: Incorrect `light_emission` handle for item models
issues.body:
### Bug Description

In [net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/immediate/model/BakedModelEncoder.java#L33](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/dev/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/immediate/model/BakedModelEncoder.java#L33), the second param of `getLightCoordsWithEmission()` requires vanilla `light_emission` which would be in range [0, 15]. But Sodium passes an encoded light coordinate for it, which would be at least 0x100010 (1048592) if `light_emission` of this quad is not zero. This will lead to any non-zero light_emission value becomes full bright on item models.

### Reproduction Steps

Create any item model with only 1 light emission, and see it's as bright as 15.

### Log File

Nothing useful in log

### Crash Report

No crash

issues.title: Translucency sorting fails for intersecting non-axis-aligned coplanar quads
issues.body: ### Bug Description In the case of terrain meshed banners in BBE, where each banner with multiple banner patterns consists of coplanar layers of translucent quads, strange sort behavior can be observed when overlapping banners (which to my understanding attempts quad splitting). There was a patch implemented to fix previous issues where coplanar quads were not taken into account at all, which can be found [here](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/pull/3480/changes/5e5ad775b873a3ac088857b5f7e2c3f8cbf54208) but I suspect this does not apply when quad splitting is necessary Example edge case where sorting fails (intersecting, splitting): Normal working case (non intersecting, no splitting): ### Reproduction Steps 1. Load BBE (please use the latest version from [actions](https://github.com/EdeenMC/betterblockentities/actions/runs/25528081943) as it implements patches related to banners fixing issues on our part) along with Sodium either latest on `dev` (will require an update of a mixin) which got "broken" in [this](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/commit/a327f636280015ae9103d9e605420f438c043703#diff-4bdb4606abc619455e1c13039c0ac58fa1299df8ea04046edcae54215122636c) commit, or use the latest 0.8.11 2. Stack a bunch of overlapping banners (preferably with many patterns, ominous banner is a good tester) and watch how pattern ordering becomes incorrect or causes "z-fighting" artifacts like in the first posted picture. ### Log File Nothing relevant in the log file ### Crash Report Nothing relevant in the crash report either. The issue happens on all hardware and across OpenGL versions

issues.title: Question about a potential fork/extension
issues.body:
Hi CaffeineMC, I'm planning to work on a project called Basalt, which is basically a lightweight fork of Sodium. Since you switched to the PolyForm Shield license, I wanted to check in with you guys before I actually put anything online to make sure I’m not breaking any rules.
The idea is to refactor the entity rendering pipeline using an Entity Component System (ECS) approach. Right now the object-oriented way Minecraft handles entities is a bit of a bottleneck, so I want to try moving that data into contiguous memory to help with CPU cache efficiency. It's more of a structural experiment than a standalone mod, so it would still need Sodium's core to actually work.
I just want to be sure you're okay with me distributing this as a derivative work. It’s strictly a performance experiment for the community, no commercial stuff or "competition" intended at all. Also, let me know how you'd prefer I handle the credits/attribution to stay 100% compliant with the new license.
Love your work, just trying to do this the right way without stepping on anyone's toes.
Cheers, TheMars

issues.title: [Performance Regression] FPS drop from 200+ to ~40 on Intel N6000 (Java 25 / MC 26.1.2)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

After updating to Sodium 0.8.10 on Minecraft 26.1.2, I am experiencing a massive performance regression. Previously, I maintained a stable 180–230 FPS, but now the game struggles to stay between 30–50 FPS using the exact same configuration and environment.

System Information
CPU: Intel Pentium Silver N6000 (Quad-core)

GPU: Intel UHD Graphics

RAM: 8GB

OS: Windows 11

Minecraft Version: 26.1.2 (Tiny Takeover)  

Loader: Fabric 0.19.2

Sodium Version: 0.8.10  

JVM Arguments
I am using the following flags which previously provided high performance on this hardware: -Xms2G -Xmx4G -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+UseStringDeduplication -XX:+UseZGC   
   


### Reproduction Steps

Steps to Reproduce
Launch Minecraft 26.1.2 with Sodium 0.8.10.

Load any world (Singleplayer or Multiplayer).

Observe FPS via F3 menu; frames are capped significantly lower than previous versions despite identical video settings.

Additional Mod Context
The issue persists with a minimal mod set, but my standard optimization stack includes:

Lithium, FerriteCore, ImmediatelyFast, Entity Culling, and More Culling.
(Note: I have tested with and without culling mods, and the regression remains tied to the Sodium update.)

Expected Behavior
Performance should be consistent with previous builds (~200 FPS), especially given the memory management improvements touted in the 0.8.x series for Java 25.

issues.title: NoSuchMethodError:long org.lwjgl.opengl.WGL.wglGetCurrentContext()` during initialization on NeoForge 1.21.5
issues.body:
### Bug Description

# [Bug]: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: wglGetCurrentContext() on NeoForge 1.21.5

### 📝 Description
The game crashes immediately during the **"Initializing game"** phase when Sodium is installed. The crash is caused by a `java.lang.NoSuchMethodError` related to LWJGL's Windows-specific context handling

---

### 💻 Environment
*   **🎮 Minecraft:** 1.21.5
*   **🛠️ Loader:** NeoForge 21.5.97
*   **⚡ Mod:** Sodium v0.6.13+mc1.21.5 (also reproducible on v0.6.12)
*   **📦 LWJGL:** 3.4.1+2
*   **🚀 Launcher:** Prism Launcher
*   **🖥️ OS:** Windows 11 25H2 (KB5083631) (26200.8328)
*   **📟 GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (Driver v582.28)

---

### 📋 Steps to Reproduce
1.  Set up a **clean** NeoForge 21.5.97 instance for Minecraft 1.21.5.
2.  Download the latest Sodium for NeoForge (v0.6.13+mc1.21.5).
3.  Place only the Sodium JAR file into the `mods` folder.
4.  Launch the game.

---

### ❌ Actual Result
The game crashes before reaching the title screen with the following error:
`java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'long org.lwjgl.opengl.WGL.wglGetCurrentContext()'`

---

### 🔍 Technical Analysis
*   **Point of Failure:** The stack trace points to Sodium's `workarounds.context_creation.RenderSystemMixin`
*   **Root Cause:** Sodium attempts to call `WGL.wglGetCurrentContext()`, but this method is missing or not mapped in the **LWJGL 3.4.1+2** version provided by the environment
*   **Isolation:** The issue persists in a clean environment with no other mods, confirming this is a direct incompatibility between Sodium's NeoForge build and the current LWJGL/NeoForge setup

---

### ⚠️ Impact
This issue **completely blocks** the usage of Sodium on NeoForge 1.21.5 for Windows users. Despite the Modrinth release notes claiming improved compatibility, the base functionality is broken due to this missing method

---

### ✅ Workaround
*   Removing Sodium allows the game to launch normally.
*   Potential alternative: **Embeddium** (once updated/available for 1.21.5).

---
**Relevant Crash Log Segment:**
```java
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'long org.lwjgl.opengl.WGL.wglGetCurrentContext()'
    at net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderSystem.handler$zkk000$sodium$postContextReady(RenderSystem.java:1234)
    ...
```

### Reproduction Steps

## 📂 Reproduction Steps

1. Create Instance: Set up a clean Minecraft 1.21.5 instance using a launcher such as Prism Launcher or the official launcher.  
2. Install Loader: Download and install NeoForge 21.5.97 for Minecraft 1.21.5 from the official NeoForge website.  
3. Download Mod: Obtain the latest Sodium for NeoForge (v0.6.13+mc1.21.5) from its official page on CurseForge (e.g., version "Sodium 0.6.13 for NeoForge - B - Apr 4, 2025") or Modrinth.  
4. Install Mod: Place only the downloaded sodium-neoforge-0.6.13+mc1.21.5.jar file into the mods folder of the newly created profile.  
5. Launch: Start the game and observe the crash during the initialization phase.

issues.title: Vanilla particle shaders intermittently read all uniforms as 0 (Globals + DynamicTransforms UBOs)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

### Summary
At certain world positions / camera rotations, vanilla particles drawn through `assets/minecraft/shaders/core/particle.fsh` see most uniforms from the `Globals` and `DynamicTransforms` UBOs read as `0`. Other render paths (entities, terrain, GUI) are unaffected. I've observed this bug on both of my PCs, a 3060 + i510600k build and a 3070 + intel i7 7820x build, meaning it's a bit less likely to be due to a specific driver or setup issue.

### Key findings (observed)
- Certain world positions + camera rotations cause most tested uniforms from the `Globals` and `DynamicTransforms` UBOs to read as `0`. Which are affected seems to be inconsistent, however GameTime is consisntently affected in every instance.
- Which spots are affected can change - sometimes after a pack reload, occasionally a previously-broken spot becomes fine on its own, though that's rare.
- Whether uniforms read correctly is inconsistent between game instances. Reloading the game or world can yield different results- sometimes uniforms are populated most of the time, sometimes they're almost always `0`.
- The player's FOV also influences it - changing FOV can make broken areas start working, or vice versa.
- The freeze isn't isolated to the particle fragment shader - it affects upstream pipeline stages too. Uniform reads in assets/minecraft/shaders/include/*.glsl includes (which run before particle fsh) showed the same zeroed values in the same broken positions. Whatever leaves the UBO bindings in a bad state happens before the particle shader runs; however, it somehow only affects the particles.
- For example, a `projection.glsl` edit that applies a transform only on the 0th tick (gated by `GameTime`) causes particles to stay stuck in the transformed state forever, while everything else cycles correctly. In certain working spots, particles start cycling normally again.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Minecraft 1.21.11, Sodium mc1.21.11-0.8.7 (also reproduces on 0.8.10), Fabric Loader 0.19.2, Fabric API only - no other mods required.
2. Resource pack overriding `assets/minecraft/shaders/core/particle.fsh` with this debug shader (turns particles white when uniforms read correctly, turns particles black with zeroed UBO field):

[Gametime uniform particle test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27150298/Gametime.uniform.particle.test.zip)

```glsl
#version 330

#moj_import <minecraft:globals.glsl>

uniform sampler2D Sampler0;

in vec2 texCoord0;
in vec4 vertexColor;

out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
    vec4 color = texture(Sampler0, texCoord0) * vertexColor;
    if (color.a < 0.1) discard;

    // White = GameTime is reading correctly.
    // Black = GameTime is zeroed (bug firing on this fragment).
    fragColor = (GameTime == 0.0) ? vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
                                  : vec4(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0);
}
```
3. Spawn any particles and look around. In broken positions, particles render black, meaning that the GameTime uniform is broken and passing 0. In positions where it works, the particles render white.

4. Test on vanilla to observe the correct behaviour, all particles render white.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27150517/latest.log)

**This could be relevant?**
```
[21:19:45] [Render thread/INFO]: Resizing Dynamic Transforms UBO, capacity limit of 2 reached during a single frame. New capacity will be 4.
[21:19:45] [Render thread/INFO]: Resizing Dynamic Transforms UBO, capacity limit of 4 reached during a single frame. New capacity will be 8.
[21:19:46] [Render thread/INFO]: Resizing Dynamic Transforms UBO, capacity limit of 8 reached during a single frame. New capacity will be 16.
```

issues.title: back face culling optimisation
issues.body:
### Request Description

# Feature Proposal: CPU-Side Directional Back-Face Culling Before Mesh Submission



**Category:** Rendering Optimisation

**Estimated Gain:** ~20% reduction in submitted geometry in normal gameplay



## Summary



This proposal suggests filtering chunk mesh triangles based on the player's current look direction **on the CPU, before the mesh is submitted to Sodium for rendering**. Faces whose normals point in the same direction as the player's look direction are invisible to the player and can be safely removed from the mesh prior to GPU submission, reducing rendering overhead.



## Problem



Sodium already performs **block face culling** (removing shared faces between adjacent solid blocks) and relies on the GPU rasterizer for standard back-face culling. However, at the chunk mesh level, faces that are geometrically facing *away* from the player's look direction are still included in the mesh sent to the GPU. These faces will never be visible in that frame and is vram wasted.



## Proposed Solution

### My Idea to fix this


Btw the format of storing a normal is memory unefficient,and to do the later modifications I think we need to do this

In my mod I have implemented it by changing normal format to 4bits

In binary->

1 = up

01 = down

11 = west

001 = east

101 = south

111 = north



Before giving a chunk mesh to the GPU to render, we filter the triangles that we cant see using the player's look direction:



1. We get the player's look direction** — Minecraft already records this every tick, so no .

2. Encode it as a 3/4-bit binary value (to do the && operations faster) — There are 6 axis-aligned face directions (±X, ±Y, ±Z), which fit in 4/3 bits.

3.Each triangle/face in the chunk mesh also has a 4-bit normal encoded at build time, representing which way its normal points.

4.Apply a bitwise AND between the player encoded direction bits and the triangle direction bits

5.If the result is true -> the face is pointing directly away from the player's view → remove it from the skip the submission submission.



Some sudo code ->

Function to ->

playerDirBits = encode4Bit(player.lookDirection) 



for each triangle in chunkMesh:

if (triangle.directionBits && playerDirBits)= true:

skip triangle subbmision 

else:

include in submittedMesh



### Diagram





Faces whose normals align with the player's look direction are the ones facing away from the camera — the player can never see them in that frame.



---



## Expected Performance Gain



- In a normal closed/open environment, roughly **2 out of 6 face directions** are pointing away from the player at any given time.

- This translates to approximately **~20% less geometry** submitted to the GPU per frame.

- The gain is most seen **indoors, in caves, or in dense builds**, and lower in open terrain where many faces are visible.

- also in mountain areas it is more.

---


## Implementation Notes from my previous mod


### Where to Hook In

- The filter should run in the ** pre-mesh-submission stage**, after chunk mesh compilation but before GPU buffer upload.

- Player look direction is already available in the Minecraft client tick — no new data needs to be recorded.


### Execution Options

| **CPU (bitwise AND loop)** | Very fast; simple integer ops on the direction array |

| **GPU compute shader** | Could parallelise the filter across all triangles at once |

Both options can be done. The CPU method is easier to set up, and the bitwise AND is very cheap per triangle.



### Update Frequency
- The filter does **not** need to run every frame. It only needs to re-run when the player's look direction **crosses a face-direction threshold** (e.g. shifts from "mostly north" to "mostly east").

- This avoids per-frame mesh rebuilding cost and keeps overhead minimal.



### Direction Encoding (4-bit scheme)

```

Bit 0 = +X face

Bit 1 = -X face

Bit 2 = +Y face

Bit 3 = -Y face

(+Z / -Z handled via the remaining bits or a 6-bit variant)

```



---



## Differences from Existing Sodium Culling



| Feature | What it removes | When |

|---|---|---|

| Block Face Culling (existing) | Shared faces between adjacent solid blocks | At mesh build time |

| Fog Occlusion (existing) | Chunks beyond fog distance | Per frame |

| **This proposal** | Faces pointing same direction as player look | Per look-direction threshold change |



This is **additive** — it works on top of existing culling, not as a replacement.



--- ## Concerns / Open Questions - **Non-axis-aligned geometry:** Custom block models with diagonal faces would need their normals sorted into the nearest axis direction or handled separately.

- **Mesh rebuild cost:** If re-filtering is triggered too frequently (e.g. every tick), it may negate the gain. Threshold-based filtering may be needed

-if a system is cpu limited then this would be worse for performance.



---



## Summary



A simple, low-cost CPU-side directional filter applied to chunk meshes before GPU submission could eliminate ~20% of rendered geometry with minimal cpu/gpu overhead. The core operation is a 4-bit AND per triangle, triggered only on significant look-direction changes, using data Minecraft already tracks.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Permanent Legacy OpenGL Toggle for Unsupported Hardware

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

issues.body:
### Request Description

With the introduction of the experimental Vulkan rendering backend in Minecraft 26.2 Snapshot 1, Mojang has signaled a long-term transition away from OpenGL. While the vanilla client currently includes a "Graphics API" toggle, there is concern within the legacy hardware community that this toggle may eventually be removed in favor of an automatic fallback system.

I am requesting that Sodium maintains a permanent, manual toggle for the OpenGL and Vulkan backends within its own internal "Advanced" video settings.

Reasoning
Hardware Compatibility: Many users are on legacy integrated graphics (e.g., Intel HD 4000 series / Ivy Bridge) that physically lack Vulkan support but run OpenGL 4.6 efficiently.

Performance Stability: On newer low-power hardware like the Intel Pentium Silver N6000, Vulkan may offer higher peak FPS, but OpenGL often provides more consistent frametimes and stability with current mod stacks.

Mod Parity: Sodium's strength is its custom rendering pipeline. Having a manual toggle ensures that users can force the backend that works best with their specific driver version (e.g., Intel's 2020 legacy drivers) without relying on vanilla's automatic detection, which can sometimes fail.

Additional Context
Testing on Minecraft 26.1.2 with Sodium shows stable performance at 200+ FPS on OpenGL. Maintaining this toggle in future versions (26.2+) will prevent hardware-specific crashes during the transition to "Vibrant Visuals" and ensure the mod remains accessible to the millions of players on older laptop hardware.

issues.title: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION crash on B580, glGetString returns null in GlContextInfo.create()
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Sodium crashes the game immediately on startup with a fatal JVM access violation when calling glGetString inside GlContextInfo.create(). The B580's OpenGL driver appears to return a null pointer for glGetString(GL_VENDOR), which Sodium does not null-check before dereferencing, causing a native crash outside the JVM with no recovery possible.

Expected behavior: Sodium should handle a null return value from glGetString gracefully, or throw a caught Java exception with a useful error message rather than a fatal native crash.

Removing Sodium allows the game to launch, confirming it as the sole cause of the crash.

Mods installed: fabric-api 0.119.4+1.21.4, iris 1.8.8+mc1.21.4, lithium 0.15.3+mc1.21.4, sodium 0.6.13+mc1.21.4, modernfix 5.20.3+mc1.21.4, immediatelyfast 1.8.6+1.21.4, ferritecore 7.1.3

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install Sodium 0.6.13+mc1.21.4 on Fabric Loader 0.18.6 with Minecraft 1.21.4
2. Ensure the system has an Intel Arc B580 GPU with driver version 32.0.101.8626 (latest available as of April 2026)
3. Launch the game
4. Game crashes immediately before reaching the main menu with a fatal JVM access violation

Note: The "-Dorg.lwjgl.opengl.Display.allowSoftwareOpenGL=true" JVM argument does not prevent the crash.

Replace the framerate slider with a numeric input for custom FPS caps
issues.body:
### Request
Would you consider replacing Sodium's framerate limit slider with a numeric text box and allowing arbitrary positive FPS caps?

### Why this would help
- The current 10-step slider is awkward when someone wants an exact cap like 144, 165, 180, 240, 360, or 480.
- The old 260 ceiling means anything above that effectively becomes uncapped instead of staying at a real user-defined limit.
- A typed value makes more sense here than a slider because this is usually an exact-match setting, not something people tune by feel.

### Expected behavior
- The framerate option accepts any positive integer cap.
- Values above the current 260 limit are treated as real caps instead of "max" or uncapped.
- The chosen value saves through the normal options flow and stays in sync anywhere the vanilla framerate option is changed.

### Extra context
I ended up building a small addon for this behavior on my own setup, and after actually using it for a while it feels much better than the slider in practice.

I also noticed draft PR #2618 touches the same area, so this might overlap with work you've already seen.

labels.name: B-LTS
labels.description: Branch: Only relevant for LTS, unapplicable on current

issues.body:
### Bug Description

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0d6d951-58e0-4cb3-99a9-f14be5da3cdf)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/723a9322-6423-49ea-92ad-92ef4589d291)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc2c3963-f2aa-40ef-bc3f-ab7436f3f986)

Dear Minecraft Mod Developers and Support Team,

I am writing to report a rendering bug that occurs when using four specific mods together in Minecraft 1.20.1. The issue affects the rendering of block entities, causing significant visual glitches that disrupt gameplay.

Basic Information

- Minecraft Version: 1.20.1

- Mod Loader: Fabric (latest compatible version for 1.20.1)

- Affected Mods (all latest compatible versions for 1.20.1):
        

  - Valkyrien Skies

  - Sodium

  - Litematica

  - Indium

- System Information: No hardware-related issues; the bug is reproducible on multiple devices with different specifications.

Bug Description

When the four aforementioned mods are installed and enabled simultaneously, block entities (specifically container and functional blocks) fail to render in their correct in-game positions. Instead, these block entities renderdirectly above the game camera and follow all camera movements (e.g., turning, looking up/down, moving the player). This creates a persistent visual glitch that makes it impossible to interact with the affected blocks normally and severely impacts the overall gameplay experience.

Affected block entities include, but are not limited to:

- Chests (all types)

- Ender Chests

- Beds (all colors)

- Doors (wooden and iron, both open and closed states)

- Other container/functional block entities (e.g., furnaces, crafting tables) may also be affected, but the above are the most consistently problematic.

Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Minecraft 1.20.1 with the latest compatible Fabric loader.

2. Install the latest versions of Valkyrien Skies, Sodium, Litematica, and Indium (all compatible with 1.20.1 and Fabric).

3. Launch Minecraft and create a new single-player world (or load an existing one).

4. Place any of the affected block entities (e.g., a chest, bed, or door) in the world.

5. Observe the block entity: it will not render in its placed position, but instead will appear floating above the camera.

6. Move the camera (turn left/right, look up/down) – the glitched block entity will move in sync with the camera, remaining above it at all times.

Additional Notes

- The bug only occurs when all four mods are enabled together. Disabling any one of the four mods resolves the rendering issue, and block entities render correctly in their intended positions.

- I have tested this issue with no other mods installed (only the four listed above) to rule out conflicts with other modifications, and the bug persists consistently.

- This issue appears similar to existing rendering conflicts between Valkyrien Skies, Litematica, and Sodium reported in previous mod versions, but this specific combination with Indium and Minecraft 1.20.1 has not been documented in detail.

- No error messages appear in the game log or console when the bug occurs; the issue is purely visual.

Expected Behavior

Block entities should render in their correct placed positions in the world, independent of camera movement, when using the four mods together – consistent with their behavior when any one of the mods is disabled.

I hope this report helps identify and resolve the conflict between these mods. Please let me know if any additional information, such as mod version numbers or screenshots/videos of the bug, is needed to assist with troubleshooting.

Thank you for your hard work in maintaining and improving these mods.

Sincerely,

A Minecraft Player

issues.title: Transparent blocks pushed over chunk border flicker
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Transparent blocks (including slabs, glass, stairs, trapdoors...) flicker when being pushed across a chunk border via a piston or sticky piston. The block only disappears as it is pushed across the chunk border and not when it is pulled back. This bug occurs regardless of which chunk the player is standing in. Additionally, this bug does not affect solid blocks. Redstone clock speed seems to have some effect with slower clocks being able to reproduce the bug more effectively. Other means of powering the piston including levers and buttons seem to inconsistently produce the bug as well.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a54ab393-43b4-4ba2-88bc-3610d2d17556


This bug only occurs if the redstone clock powering the piston does not interact with or cross into the neighboring chunk. The video below shows the relevant redstone clock "interacting" with the other chunk (even though it does not cross into it) which fixes the bug.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd39d5d5-d100-46ea-a746-5ea4711b5b54


Redstone updates caused by other clocks in the neighboring chunk have no effect on fixing the bug. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdaa0a81-743b-4f3c-9b71-96dfaef6c1c1

This bug was found using Minecraft version 1.21.11, Fabric 0.18.2, and Sodium 0.8.6 with Sodium being the only mod installed. This bug is not present when Sodium is uninstalled.

### Reproduction Steps

- Open Minecraft with fabric-loader-0.18.2-1.21.11 with Sodium 0.8.6 in the mods folder
- Build a slow redstone clock powering a sticky piston that is able to push/pull a translucent block between two chunks (have the block travel across a chunk border)
- Make sure that no part of the redstone clock powering the piston interacts with the chunk that the block is being pushed into
- The translucent block should flicker out of existence as it is pushed across the chunk border, but will appear in the neighboring chunk until it is pulled back to its original position

Most probably needs a OS check before adding AMD_GAME_OPTIMIZATION_BROKEN to the list of Workarounds. Note that the game does not crash so the workaround does not actually try to apply (see comment above), so this a misleading warning and a low priority issue. 

I am in a AMD GPU system, but given that it does not care about OS type before printing warning, it might as well not care about GPU vendor, so additional checks might be needed to ensure warning only gets printed if the workaround is actually applied.

The no error context unsupported warning existed previously so is not the focus of this issue.

Launch MC 1.21.11 with Sodium 0.8.6 in a Linux Mesa system

issues.title: Adaptive refresh rate displays cause large frame-time spikes to appear when (only after) alt-tabbing between windows.
issues.body: ### Bug Description The above images were taken with G-Sync enabled in the Nvidia control panel, and adaptive refresh rate 'on' in monitor settings. Notice how the frequent frame-time spikes appear after alt-tabbing. The above images were taken with G-Sync DISABLED in the Nvidia control panel, and adaptive refresh rate 'OFF' in monitor settings. No more repetitive frame-time spikes when changing contexts. I'm not sure why this issue only appears after changing contexts, were the behaviour is otherwise fine on the initial launch state. I also noticed that the amplitude of those spikes were related to the setting 'CPU Render Ahead' where as the frequency was related to how saturated the graphics pipeline was, i.e if DH / Shaders were disabled, the spikes would still appear but at a much more spaced rate. Also I was iterating through the in-game sync settings to see if it had any effect which it didn't so ignore the V-Sync enabled in the top left. Should also note that in windowed mode the performance was significantly degraded too. Even without switching contexts. ### Reproduction Steps - Enable G-Sync / Freesync (?) in respective control panel + monitor settings. - Launch game in Fullscreen. - Inspect frame-time graph in-game after it's settled. - Alt-tab, and re-inspect the graph, check if periodic spikes appear. ### Log File [20260225-9.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25558978/20260225-9.json.gz) ### Crash Report [crash-2026-02-25_22.03.38-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25559149/crash-2026-02-25_22.03.38-client.txt)

issues.title: Incorrect assumption that buffer size matches the stride of primitive vertex count
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Starting Sodium 0.7.3, it is not guaranteed anymore that `(gl_VertexID % 4)` matches exactly with the quad boundary. This does not seem to visibly affect Sodium, but affects Iris shaders that rely on this. 
After investigating, [this commit](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/commit/7fd731ecd3a9589cc557d2f9799ce1df8082f208) exposed an underlying issue with the way Sodium handles rendering. In particular, the size estimate may not be aligned to a multiple of 4 anymore. While this shouldn't matter, as the geometry still fits in this buffer, it seems that Sodium relies on the byte size of the buffer instead of the actual geometry count. 

A bandaid fix is to round up the new capacity estimate to make sure it is divisible by 4: however this does not fix the underlying issues.

issues.title: Screen freezes while game logic continues when using Sodium + Entity Culling (tickCulling)
issues.body:
Screen freezes while game logic continues when using Sodium + Entity Culling

(I did all the deskription with AI beckause i do not know english good, but it is all trye)
Sometimes the entire screen freezes, but the game itself keeps running.

I can still move, place blocks, attack, etc.

Other players see me moving normally.

If I press Escape, I can hover over buttons and the cursor changes as if the menu is open, but the image on screen does not update.

There is no crash and the client shuts down cleanly if I quit.

So it looks like only the rendering / display is stuck, while the game loop continues.

This only happens on heavier survival / modded servers (Create + Botania etc.) after ~10–15 minutes of play or during intense fights. On a very lightweight PvP server with almost no extra blocks/entities I never see this freeze.

I am using the Entity Culling mod together with Sodium. With this configuration in config/entityculling.json:

"tickCulling": true,
"skipEntityCulling": false,
"skipBlockEntityCulling": false,
"blockEntityFrustumCulling": true,
"forceDisplayCulling": false
the issue is reproducible.

After changing only:

"tickCulling": false
and restarting the game, the freezes completely stopped on the same servers and in the same scenarios.

The freeze did also happen (but less often) before I installed Entity Culling, which is why I believe Sodium’s CullThread is involved. With tickCulling=true the problem becomes very easy to reproduce, so it looks like Sodium’s culling and Entity Culling’s tick‑based culling are amplifying the same underlying issue on worlds with lots of entities.

### Reproduction Steps

Launch Minecraft 1.21.11 with Fabric and Sodium 0.8.4.

Install Entity Culling (latest for 1.21.x) and play on a survival/modded server that uses content mods like Create and Botania (many entities and block entities).

In config/entityculling.json, set:

"tickCulling": true,
"skipEntityCulling": false,
"skipBlockEntityCulling": false,
"blockEntityFrustumCulling": true,
"forceDisplayCulling": false
Join the server and play for 10–20 minutes, especially in areas with many contraptions, mobs, particles and projectiles (for example, during duels).

At some point the screen will freeze, while input and game logic still work (you can move, others see you moving, you can open the menu but the image does not update).

Close the game; the log only shows a clean shutdown, with CullThread shutting down and no stack trace.



### Log File

Relevant end of the log after closing the game right after a freeze:

issues.title: Fog occlusion distance slider
issues.body:
### Request Description

Because as of right now fog occlusion completely overrides view distance.
We could say view distance is now useless.

View distance in minecraft always represented the number of chunks that were loaded horizontally, due to performance limitations.

Well now it seems fog culling distance made it's way into view distance.|
Even tho we want to see the ground at high altitudes....
Fog occlusion is meant to be a performance optimisation...
But when playing on servers where the view distance is small, it ruins the rendering experience..
Players with low end pcs cannot see down into caves... Cannot see their base in the air... Can see the sky while underground !

I propose a block culling distance slider to fix most of our issues. Sliding to the max will turn it OFF.

issues.title: Vanilla enhancement/bug fix : Fog culling is a box moving according to camera orientation, not a sphere

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

issues.body: ### Bug Description First, this leads to useless dynamic calculations of what should be culled and what should not. Second, this leads to culling being further out in the box's corners, making us see further down when looking at a 45 degrees angle than straight down. I strongly believe the right approach to fog culling (which is basically just culling everything behind XX blocks of distance), would be to at least have a sphere which does not need to rotate around the player's head. Additionnaly, we could have a setting to set to the vanilla behavior if really anyone cares about having bad code into their game. Looking at 45 degrees allows us to see further which makes no sense : Looking straight down we cannot see anything. ### Reproduction Steps Reach fog culling distance, look straight down and at 45 degrees angle down. MC 1.21.4 Sodium 0.6.13 ### Log File logs ### Crash Report crash

issues.title: Disable fog occlusion setting doesn't work
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Minecraft 1.21.4,
Sodium 0.6.13,
fabric 0.17.3.

Fog occlusion cannot be turned off.
In this case I have a server which will sometimes change it's fog distance values, leading to crazy occlusion scenarios.

Flying with an elytra ? Your day is ruined. Want to appreciate the great renders sodium is providing ? Not today.

### Reproduction Steps

Play minecraft like a player would, not like a remunerated modder.

### Log File

Logs ? Logs ! This issue has been brought out by many people over many ways but no one specifically wrote this exact issue.

If fog occlusion shouldnt be disable, at least remove the setting so modders know that someone somewhere has to make a fix for it because the latest version where someone made a fix I know of is 1.20

### Crash Report

I would like not to do that either.
I mean, the dev knows about the issue and simply called it vanilla behavior, I am trying to change his mind.

I'd like to remember everyone that this mod originally was inspired from optifine ?
Optifine's goal wasn't to copy mojang or else we'd be swimming in the same shit twice....
We don't want to swim in shit.

No one cares it was possibly in the game for some versions, my fog is disabled and my fog occlusion is too.
This is render we're talking about not gameplay.

Additionnaly to not rendering half the map, server side changes to the fog distance value will cause the whole rendering to FLICKER.

This means it's not just far away terrain that's messed up, it's the whole game experience.

issues.body:
### Request Description

version: mc1.21.11-0.8.2-fabric

On invocation of `GuiGraphics.renderItem` this method is called, and creates new `int[]`. In my game profiler this init allocated 40.38GB and the whole game took 239.57GB. There should be a way to reuse these arrays.

issues.body:
### Request Description

I very much like having the overworld atmospheric fog it makes everything feel warmer; however with the new 1.21.11 update forcing nether fog to a certain distance regardless of render distance, I am literally getting lost going in a straight line unless I turn off atmospheric fog. So if its possible a separate slider specifically for the nether fog would be  amazing so that while in the nether I could see, and while in the overworld I could still have my atmospheric fog.

issues.title: The name of the "General" tab is not translatable

labels.name: F-good-first-issue
labels.description: Flag: Good first issue for new contributors

issues.body:
### Request Description

The name of the "General" tab cannot be translated using the translation key because it simply does not exist.
If I understand correctly, this is because `Component.literal` (prints the text as is) is used instead of `Component.translatable` (uses the translation key) in the string `var generalPage = builder.createOptionPage().setName(Component.literal("General"));` in the `SodiumConfigBuilder.java` class.
So I suggest using something like `var generalPage = builder.createOptionPage().setName(Component.translatable("sodium.options.pages.general"));`.

I could create a pull request, but I'm not sure what I'm suggesting is correct.

issues.title: Lighting updates appear inconsistent occasionally over chunk borders
issues.body: ### Bug Description When placing and removing light sources near the positive edge of a mostly empty chunk, that chunk will sometimes not be lit correctly until it's mesh is otherwise updated. Update: this seems to also apply to some of the neighboring blocks as well, the rules as to what it applies to aren't fully clear. This issue presents both with and without Iris and LambDynamicLights, and is especially egregious with LambDynamicLights. I've seen and confirmed this issue on 1.21.1 and 1.21.11 so far, and I did confirm all mods installed are fully up-to-date (Sodium 0.6.13, Iris 1.8.8, LambDynamicLights 4.8.7). Update: this issue appears with no other mods installed, including Fabric API. It also applies in Minecraft 1.21.11. ### Reproduction Steps Use Sodium 0.6.13+mc1.21.1 or 0.8.2+mc1.21.11 on fabric Generate an empty world (or generate the void flat preset and remove all surrounding blocks). Place a block at -1 0 -1 (or any position relative on a grid of 16 blocks), and place a block horizontally adjacent to it inside of any neighboring chunk. Place a torch on this block and remove it until the incorrect lighting appears. Alternatively, install LambDynamicLights and move around near the block while holding a bright item, and it will flicker and sometimes be left in the wrong state when you move away or remove your light source item. ### Log File [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24382255/latest.log) Second log file with no additional mods installed: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24387321/latest.log) Additional log file in Minecraft 1.21.11: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24387396/latest.log) ### Crash Report [crash-2025-12-30_06.43.58-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24382260/crash-2025-12-30_06.43.58-client.txt) Second crash report with no additional mods installed: [crash-2025-12-30_13.54.18-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24387359/crash-2025-12-30_13.54.18-client.txt) Additional crash report in Minecraft 1.21.11: [crash-2025-12-30_14.03.10-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24387403/crash-2025-12-30_14.03.10-client.txt)

issues.title: Request for Legacy Driver Support in Sodium
issues.body:
### Request Description

i hope you are doing well. First, let me thank you for making Sodium it has been instrumental in enhancing Minecraft gameplay for many players, and I really admire the effort you put into it.

i would like to know if it is possible to add support for Intel graphics driver version 10.18.1069. My laptop can only work with this driver version being capped by the manufacturer HP even though it should technically be able to be updated, and because of the economic situation in my country, I cannot upgrade to a newer system rn.

since Sodium is driver incompatible for just one version beyond what my driver currently supports, I was thinking if there could be a way to extend compatibility or create a fallback mode for users like me. Even if support were only partially, it would be great since I use Minecraft for both fun and community engagement.

I get that you have limited development resources and that supporting older hardware may not be a priority. But I still wanted to contact you to see if there is a possible workaround or if you could direct me to any other solutions.

Thank you

See user report here: https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1454570451862032394

I have a reproduction using [this world](https://www.patreon.com/c/waxfraud/posts?utm_source=campaign-search-results&vanity=waxfraud) and [this resource pack](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/3dvanilla) on `dev`. 

Analysis: The exception [at this line](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/blob/65db4b66625336fde92c37e50ec4c2868cef8c2e/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/chunk/translucent_sorting/bsp_tree/InnerPartitionBSPNode.java#L830) is being thrown because earlier at [this check](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/65db4b66625336fde92c37e50ec4c2868cef8c2e/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/render/chunk/translucent_sorting/bsp_tree/InnerPartitionBSPNode.java#L651) I mistakenly assumed there could be no quads where the `onPlaneMap` is `0110`, but this can be the case for when bent quads are split in a very particular way like this: https://www.desmos.com/3d/vuvamwcupk

The solution is to simply account for this special case in splitting and generate one degenerate quad triangle for the quad triangle that's on the inside and split the triangle that's crossing through the split plane. This is equivalent to one of the regular "vertex being clipped off of a quad resulting in a triangle and a pentagon" mode.

issues.title: Fullscreen Resolution setting is arbitrarily disabled on Linux even though it is functional
issues.body: ### Bug Description (This issue is reposted from https://github.com/Fabulously-Optimized/fabulously-optimized/issues/1053 there may be more information there) In 0.7.3, Sodium had a Fullscreen Resolution setting, but claimed it was only supported on Windows. Despite using a Linux-based OS (MX-25 w/ Xfce), this setting worked without any issue. But now, in 0.8.2, the setting cannot be changed despite the fact that it works flawlessly. This change seemingly exists for no reason other than to make the experience worse for Linux users. (truncated fastfetch report) OS: MX 25 Infinity x86_64 Kernel: Linux 6.12.57+deb3-amd64 Display: 1280x1024 @ 75 Hz DE: Xfce4 4.20 WM: Xfwm4 (X11) ### Reproduction Steps 1. Be using Linux 2. open the game 3. go to Settings 4. go to Video Settings 5. Fullscreen Resolution option is greyed out?? 6. Press Shift+P to get to vanilla video settings 7. Fullscreen Resolution can be changed ### Log File [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24347332/latest.log) ### Crash Report [crash-2025-12-26_08.05.12-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24347336/crash-2025-12-26_08.05.12-client.txt)

issues.title: [BUG] [NEOFORGE 1.21.1] Sodium forces the deadlock on a world when GLFW-Wayland AND C2ME is used alongside it
issues.body:
### Bug Description

I found this out absolutely randomly. I swear I don't know how this works, but that's the thing:
Since I despise Xorg and Minecraft, basically, works via XWayland, I decided to make it more native thanks to GLFW-Wayland. Before, though, it was fine, but now, if Sodium, C2ME and GLFW-Wayland are used together, the world loads, but before showing any picture, Sodium crashes (and it's exactly Sodium crashing, which was found out thanks to Not Enough Crashes). And, just in case, it doesn't apply when creating a new world - when you do, it works fine, but after you re-enter the world, it results to what's described above.

System/Hardware:
Laptop: Lenovo ideapad Y700-15ISK
CPU: Intel Core i5-6300HQ
GPU (that's used in the game): Nvidia GeForce GTX 960M (with __GL_THREAD_OPTIMIZATIONS=0 flag due to it not working otherwise)
RAM: 16 GB (8 GB allocated for the game)
Launcher used: Fjord Launcher
OS: Arch Linux
Compositor: Hyprland (may be of use, Idk)

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install latest NeoForge instance for 1.21.1
2. Install Sodium and a few additions to it (Sodium Extra, Reese's Sodium Options, Substrate)
3. Install C2ME alongside it
4. Select GLFW-Wayland as the custom GLFW instance in Minecraft instance's options
5. Try entering a world that was created with this combo used and (according to Crash Assistant) receive a deadlock (40001 ms delay)

Countermeasure:
Disable either C2ME or GLFW-Wayland

issues.title: Sodium 0.8.0 Renderer Fails to Register on Minecraft Realms (MC 1.21.11)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Sodium 0.8.0 consistently crashes when connecting to Minecraft Realms with `UnsupportedOperationException: Attempted to retrieve active rendering plug-in before one was registered.` The Indigo renderer fails to register with the Fabric Renderer API before particle rendering is attempted.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install Sodium 0.8.0+mc1.21.11 with Fabric Loader 0.18.3
2. Launch Minecraft 1.21.11
3. Connect to a Minecraft Realm

milestone.title: Upcoming Minor
milestone.description: An upcoming minor release, but not necessarily the next one

issues.body:
PR that fixes some of these aspects: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/pull/3397

Potential Improvements to be made
- [x] Indicate pages that open external screens more clearly in the page list, by an icon, text, or both
- [x] Make scrollbars thicker for easier use
- [x] Hide search bar clear button when nothing is searched
- [x] Make search bar text have more contrast
- [x] Inset the whole UI into a centered container of reasonable width on large screens
- [x] When inset, space between search bar/close button and page list/search bar?
- [x] Disabled tickboxes don't show the right enablement state
- [x] per-option and global reset by holding down shift
- [x] Clicking on mod headers in the page list should jump to the start of their options in the option list
~~- [ ] Clicking on mod headers in the page list should collapse the page list, in conflict with the previous suggestion. This could also collapse the version information. However, it's bad UX to have two similar elements (mod headers and page headers) in the page list cause such different behaviors.~~
- [x] moving the window from one monitor to the other while the settings ui is open causes a crash because it tries to read a video mode with an index higher than the number of video modes on the new screen
- [x] Adjust spacing in multiple places in the UI to accomodate horizontal and vertical external margins on the content area (separately)
- [ ] Use left/right bouncy text or widen the options to account for some locale requiring more width. Bouncy text is just not nice to look at while widening the options is problematic since on small screens doing so is impossible. We could potentially widen the options slightly only when there's enough space (i.e. instead of adding an inset to the sides, we first widen the options by maybe 40% at most)
- [x] Pressing the escape key when there are pending changes should perform "undo", and then pressing it again should exit the screen.
- [ ] Option text is cut off when italic
- [ ] Reconsider the size of the reset button's click target. On iris it's the whole option width, though I don't find this behavior intuitive.
- [ ] The scrollable tooltips' scroll bar appears to be broken when the tooltips are shown inline

API Improvements
- [x] Custom update flags (like renderer reload) and registering flag-related runners globally
- [x] Post-save hooks that are syntactic sugar for a unique flag per option [example](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1447940748036014222/1448278728617492543)
- [x] API for mods to open the config screen and jump to a certain page for use in mod menu integrations. [example](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1447940748036014222/1448282906144542810)
- [x] Document Option Overlay and Replacement API usage
- [ ] Graphics presets to match vanilla
- [ ] Customization of presents? Adding new presets? adding options from mods to presets through the api?
- [ ] Allow other mods to hide existing options (such as when they become inapplicable for some reason due to the other mod's changes to the game)
- [ ] Allow other mods to insert their options in a specific place, review usecase
- [ ] Allow other mods to define the order in which they appear in the sidebar
- [ ] Consider design for more flexible enum options that don't have predefined values, as per the suggestion [here](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/752637878462578778/1503876539295727817).

issues.title: VSync and frame rate instability
issues.body:
### Request Description

**Context and Problem Description**

When VSync is enabled in Minecraft (likely standard double buffering), the frame rate consistently drops from an average of **~80-100 FPS** (VSync disabled) to **~40 FPS** (VSync enabled default/adaptive).

This behavior is characteristic of VSync dropping to a divisor (60/2 = 30 FPS, or similar) due to slight, transient spikes in **frame time** (frame pacing instability), even though the average FPS is high.

**Troubleshooting Steps Attempted**

1. Tested without VSync: FPS stable at 80-100.
2. Enabled VSync in Minecraft (default/adaptive): FPS drops to ~40.
3. Forced **Triple Buffering** via the AMD driver control panel (OpenGL setting): No noticeable change in FPS stability or VSync behavior.

**Questions for Sodium Developers**

1. **VSync Overriding:** Is it true that external driver settings (like Triple Buffering from AMD/NVIDIA panel) cannot reliably override the built-in VSync settings in Minecraft (Java Edition)?
2. **Sodium's VSync:** Does the Sodium mod specifically modify or replace the functionality of the built-in Minecraft VSync, or does it primarily rely on the vanilla implementation?
3. **CPU Render-Ahead Limit:** I understand the existing CPU Render-Ahead Limit addresses CPU-side load spikes and smooths the CPU $\to$ GPU pipeline. Is this correct, and does it **not** directly address GPU-side frame time spikes that cause VSync drops?
4. **Future Feature Request:** Are there any plans to integrate or enable settings for more advanced frame pacing controls, such as forcing **OpenGL Triple Buffering** or implementing alternatives like **Fast Sync (NVIDIA)/Enhanced Sync (AMD)** equivalents?

---
*Thank you for your hard work on Sodium*

issues.title: Young-Gen Buffer for Avoiding Additional Buffer Allocations
issues.body:
https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/pull/3313 implements buffer reuse and found that it's enough to bring the number of allocated buffers back to 0.6.13 levels. However, it does not implement a young gen buffer as that's added complexity and doesn't seem to be necessary to fix the regression at the moment.

A young gen buffer could, especially for index data, provide an additional savings in required memory and buffer allocations. It doesn't seem to be necessary for collecting enough of a region's uploads to accurately estimate the required size since the implemented system does a good enough job of that already. Reducing the number of buffer allocations, and sharing buffers of small regions in particular, may further improve frame time stability during chunk loading on problematic Intel drivers.

This issue is a followup of https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3300, which contains further elaboration of this idea.

issues.title: Game crashes after input freeze triggered by rapid Alt+R presses
issues.body:
### Bug Description

I'm encountering a reproducible crash in Sodium that occurs after a specific sequence of input actions. The issue can be reliably reproduced with only Sodium installed.

I'm not entirely sure why pressing "Alt + R" sometimes triggers the crash. "Alt + R" is the hotkey I assigned in Litematica to toggle rendering on/off. Initially, I thought it was an issue with Litematica, but the problem persists even after completely uninstalling Litematica. I also tried deleting the config folder to reset all settings, yet the issue remains.

Environment:
Minecraft version: 1.21.8
Sodium version: sodium-fabric-0.7.2+mc1.21.8
Loader: Fabric 0.17.2
OS: Windows10
Java version: GraalVM 25+37.1

JVM arguments are as follows:
-Xmx4G -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:+DisableExplicitGC -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+PerfDisableSharedMem --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED

### Reproduction Steps

1. Launch Minecraft with only sodium-fabric-0.7.2+mc1.21.8 installed.
2. Enter any world (singleplayer or multiplayer).
3. Hold down the Alt key and rapidly press the R key multiple times.
4. The game may freeze all keyboard and mouse input (the window remains responsive visually, but no input is processed).
5. Use a system-level shortcut (e.g., Alt+Tab) to switch to another window, then switch back to Minecraft.
6. The game immediately crashes.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23280976/latest.log)

### Crash Report

The game crash did not generate a crash-report file—only a JVM log is available:

[hs_err_pid9888.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23280977/hs_err_pid9888.log)

issues.title: Sunlight in the overworld is not as bright as it is in the vanilla game
issues.body: ### Bug Description Minecraft 1.17 decreased the brightness of sunlight in the overworld, mostly noticeable on lower brightness settings. This was changed in 1.21.9 to make it brighter again. Sodium does not reflect this recent change, leading to a noticeable difference in the appearance of the world at daytime. I am not sure if the brightness of block light or light in other dimensions is also affected by this. Open each image in a separate tab and switch between them to see the difference more clearly. Minecraft 1.21.10: With Sodium (0.7.2 for Fabric 1.21.10): Vanilla Minecraft: Sodium: ### Reproduction Steps 1. Load a world in vanilla 1.21.10 or 1.21.9, set the game brightness to Moody, set the time to midday, and take a screenshot 2. Load the world with Sodium and take a screenshot from the same position 3. Compare the brightness of the world surface in the two screenshots ### Log File [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23147573/latest.log) ### Crash Report [crash-2025-10-26_19.05.13-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23147423/crash-2025-10-26_19.05.13-client.txt)

issues.title: Immediate-Mode Non-Terrain Optimizations
issues.body:
This is a tracking issue for a collection of optimizations that could be made to immediate-mode and non-terrain rendering in general. It combines the other heterogenous collection of issues we've had on this topic. The closing of the other issues doesn't mean these types of optimization will not be considered, but merely that we are aware that many aspects of it are slow and we don't need separate issues for each of them.

It should also be noted that other mods each already apply some optimizations to some subset of of these items already.
> ImmediatelyFast fixes all of them, except for the last two (Enchantment glint is indirectly optimized, in that ImmediatelyFast reduces the draw calls needed to render enchanted items, but enchantment glint itself isn't changed) - [RK_01](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/651120262129123330/1429967783537541173)

This issue is not intended as a list of other mods that optimize these items.

- [font rendering](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/1082)
- [glowing signs](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/794)
- [signs/text](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/350)
- [block entities & entities](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/1213)
- [items](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/1124)
- [ui text, scoreboard, chat, toolbar](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/382)
- [enchantment glint](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/2497)
- [entity glow, suggestion to use geometry for lines (?)](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/2402)

issues.title: Implement More Accurate Buffer Sizing
issues.body:
Previous to 0.7, we were allocating too large buffers on the GPU because of a bug in our size calculation. Once [we fixed this](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/commit/43f8b253ccdd71789429862f96376031d879768f), more appropriately sized buffers were being used once again, but Intel drivers seem to have issues when the buffers are resized very often, leading to terrible performance during chunk loading.
Previous issue that seems to be related to this: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3295 (new issue since the old issue is incomprehensible)
The goal is an implementation that sizes buffers such that they are resized as few times as possible while avoiding excessive (video) memory usage. I have some ideas on how to do this, which we discussed on discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/651120262129123330/1429864772941123604).

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Game is consistently crashing on Sodium for 1.21.10 when reloading chunks, sometimes opening inventory, or activating chunks,

I have removed all mods except Sodium and Fabric API to confirm, and it still happens. Not sure what is going wrong

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5476321-8560-4c22-a4a5-56e8851977a7

### Reproduction Steps

1. Load world
2. Crash.

issues.title: Display entity texture interpolation is broken

milestone.title: Upcoming Minor
milestone.description: An upcoming minor release, but not necessarily the next one

issues.body:
### Bug Description

The **display entity** of _an item that has texture interpolation_ **has no interpolation.**

An example of what it should look like **without sodium:**
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52d21e54-c578-41e3-9124-ef0a0fd8dac0

An example of what it looks like **with sodium:**
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83f3c062-ab58-4515-be08-520293639d43

### Reproduction Steps

1. Summon a display entity (item or block display) with a texture containing interpolation.
2. You see that the texture interpolation is missing. The texture simply switches between its states.

### Log File

issues.title: OPTIMIZATION IDEAS
issues.body:
### Request Description

Hello Sodium Team,

First of all, thank you for creating Sodium—it’s truly amazing, and it has completely transformed how Minecraft runs for many players like me. I really admire the work you have done, and it inspired me to think about some ideas that could further improve Minecraft performance while keeping the gameplay smooth and enjoyable.

I have drafted a blueprint for a client-side optimization mod that I believe could be valuable. The core idea is to improve frame rates, reduce unnecessary rendering, and simplify physics where possible, while keeping the experience immersive. Here is a summary of the main concepts:


---

1. Rendering Optimizations

Exposed-Only Rendering: Only render block faces visible to the player. Blocks hidden behind others or underground are rendered when exposed, such as during mining.

Distance-Based LOD (Level of Detail): Close blocks are rendered normally, while distant blocks are rendered with lower resolution or skipped entirely, reducing GPU load.

Mining-Triggered Rendering: Blocks near mining activity are rendered dynamically to improve FPS without affecting gameplay.



---

2. Physics & Entity Optimizations

Fake Falling Blocks: Blocks like sand, gravel, and dripstones appear to fall but do not simulate full physics, reducing lag in large structures. They land instantly while showing simple animation.

Items-as-Blocks Auto-Pickup: Dropped items render as simplified blocks/icons and automatically enter the player’s inventory when nearby, reducing entity overload.



---

3. Dynamic Game Controls

/pixels Command: Allows players to adjust game resolution dynamically, giving users real-time control over performance and visuals.



---

4. Implementation Notes

Platform: Minecraft Java Edition + Fabric API

Client-Side Only: To avoid server-side complications

Modular Structure: Rendering, physics, entity, and command managers

Goal: Focus on FPS improvement and smoother gameplay in large worlds or high-entity scenarios



---

I believe this mod could complement Sodium by further reducing lag and providing users with flexible options to adjust performance. I would be deeply grateful if you could consider exploring this idea. If it inspires or is used in any way, I would truly appreciate even a small mention in the credits.

Thank you very much for your time and for creating such an incredible tool for the Minecraft community. I hope this blueprint can bring another step forward in making Minecraft smoother and more enjoyable for everyone.

Best regards,
Sarthak aka powerboyee

Get the newest windows 11 build from microsoft's website, 2. Install it onto a virtual machine or physical machine, 3. Ensure the display adapter is using the microsoft basic display adapter, 4. Subscribe to the OpenGL compatibility pack from the microsoft store, 5. Install minecraft 1.21.8 with fabric loader and sodium mod present on the instance, 6. Enter any world you want, 7. Press `F3` + `1` at same time to open up pie chart or observe the sun/moon texture. ### Log File The logs can be found [here](https://mclo.gs/4giWnbD). ### Crash Report The crash report can be found [here](https://mclo.gs/Du12aZB).

issues.body: Hello there, I'm the author of LittleTiles and I ran into an issue with the shading of certain quads when Sodium is installed. I cannot tell whether this is an issue on my end or an issue of Sodium itself. That's why I ask here. LittleTiles is a bit complicated. To make it short, it generates the rendering data on its own. I tried to mirror what sodium does. This is the code responsible for the rendering and it should look exactly the same: https://github.com/CreativeMD/LittleTiles/blob/1.21/src/main/java/team/creative/littletiles/client/mod/sodium/pipeline/LittleRenderPipelineSodium.java#L221-L228 To give a bit more context. LittleTiles gets the baked model of a block and shrinks each quad to the size of the tile being displayed. Then this quad is passed on here: https://github.com/CreativeMD/LittleTiles/blob/1.21/src/main/java/team/creative/littletiles/client/mod/sodium/pipeline/LittleRenderPipelineSodium.java#L198 Here is the screenshot showing the issue. The selected blocks are all blocks from littletiles. The shading is correct for the outside blocks (meaning full quads work just fine), but the 3 ones in the middle with are filled with different shapes have the lighting issue. These quads are partially filled as they sit at the edge of the block, but do not fill the entire area. I hope I could explain it so you can understand it. Maybe we can figure out the cause? Note: Skylight does work properly, it seems to be the block light layer. In Regards CreativeMD

issues.title: [1.21.1] Top level NeoForge model data is passed to `MultiPartBakedModel` submodels

labels.name: B-LTS
labels.description: Branch: Only relevant for LTS, unapplicable on current

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Sodium intercepts rendering of blocks to go through `BlockRenderer#renderModel`. `BlockRenderer#renderModel` then obtains the model data for the given model and stores it in `AbstractBlockRenderContext#modelData`. The model is then rendered through `FabricBakedModel#emitBlockQuads` from Forgified Fabric API.
Sodium overwrites the default implementation of `FabricBakedModel#emitBlockQuads` for `BakedModel`s to redirect to `AbstractBlockRenderContext#bufferDefaultModel`. `AbstractBlockRenderContext#bufferDefaultModel` then obtains quads from the model through NeoForge's `IBakedModelExtension#getQuads`, passing `AbstractBlockRenderContext#modelData` for the model data argument.

Some models like `WeightedBakedModel`, `MultiPartBakedModel`, and NeoForge's `CompositeModel` consist of multiple submodels. These models collect model data for all submodels and store it in a special format which is then returned as the model data.
When `#getQuads` is called, these models then obtain the correct model data for each submodel and in turn call `#getQuads` on the submodels.

For most cases, this works fine.
However, Forgified Fabric API overwrites `MultiPartBakedModel#emitQuads` to directly call `#emitQuads` on all the submodels. The default implementation `#emitQuads` for these submodels then ends up calling `AbstractBlockRenderContext#bufferDefaultModel`. `#bufferDefaultModel` then calls `#getQuads` on the submodel with the model data from the `MultiPartBakedModel` model. This means each submodel gets `MultiPartBakedModel`'s special model data rather than its own model data.

As far as I can tell `MultiPartBakedModel` is the only model where this goes wrong as it is the only model where Forgified Fabric API overwrites `#emitQuads` to directly emit the submodels.

### Reproduction Steps

Create a `BakedModel` which overwrites NeoForge's `IBakedModelExtension#getModelData` and `IBakedModelExtension#getQuads`.
Use a multipart blockstate file for some block.
Overwrite one of the submodels of the multipart blockstate model to use the custom baked model.
Observer that the custom baked model's `#getQuads` receives the `MultiPartBakedModel`'s model data rather the data from its own `#getModelData`.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21419802/latest.log)

### Crash Report

[crash-2025-07-25_00.05.52-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21419805/crash-2025-07-25_00.05.52-client.txt)

issues.title: NeoForge's API is not used in `ModelBlockRenderer#renderModel` mixin
issues.body:
### Bug Description

NeoForge adds an overload to `ModelBlockRenderer#renderModel` with extra parameters for level, position, and block state. These extra parameters are then used when querying block model parts from NeoForge's `BlockStateModelExtension#collectParts` API.

Sodium mixes into and intercepts the `ModelBlockRenderer#renderModel` overload from NeoForge in [ModelBlockRendererMixin](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/02253db283e4679228ba5fbc30cfc851d17123c8/neoforge/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/mixin/features/render/model/block/ModelBlockRendererMixin.java#L69).
The mixin from Sodium ignores the additional level, position, and block state arguments and calls the vanilla `BlockStateModel#collectParts` method instead of NeoForge API.

### Reproduction Steps

Create a `BlockStateModel` which overwrites `BlockStateModelExtension#collectParts`.
Call NeoForge's overload of `ModelBlockRenderer#renderModel` with level, position, and block state arguments for the created model.
Observe that the model receives `null` for the level, position, and block state arguments.

### Log File

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21393577/latest.log)

### Crash Report

[crash-2025-07-23_20.46.53-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21393587/crash-2025-07-23_20.46.53-client.txt)

issues.title: Holding a key while moving the mouse causes mouse input to judder on Xwayland
issues.body:
### Bug Description

As the title says, holding any key while moving the mouse causes the camera to judder. Releasing that key brings smooth camera motion back. This only happens on the X11 backend; setting `env DISPLAY=` on a Wayland session makes this issue go away. Removing Sodium also solves the problem.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Start moving your mouse around (while standing still)
2. Hold any key, doesn't have to be a movement key, can even be an unbound one
3. Observe the mouse input judder
4. Stop holding that key
5. Observe smooth mouse input

issues.title: Option to disable pojav crash in mixins config
issues.body:
### Request Description

Now that Pojav has the MobileGLUES and LTW renderers, and the Amethyst project (pojav's successor) is working on a rewrite to improve stuff, I think adding an option in the config to disable the pojav crash is reasonable. This way, there's less people who don't try to troubleshoot and immediately post an issue since it just crashes by default like it has been, but for the people who do, they can just disable the crash in the config file.

issues.title: Support for the development key binds.

labels.name: E-will-not-fix
labels.description: Closed: This will not be worked on

issues.body:
### Request Description

I would like to suggest adding support for the SectionPath, SectionVisibility, and Frustum culling Octree key binds. These tools are used by Mojang to make the game. However, they are currently broken since Sodium does not support them. If you try to use them, nothing will be displayed (https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3176).

Although these are not registered by default, they can be unlocked using my patch (https://github.com/Mickey42302/JavaEditionDevTools). Support for these would be a nice feature; it would allow users to enjoy both the performance improvements of Sodium and the freedom to explore the F3 key binds Mojang hides from the public.
